Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [16th April] 

events.

Today's Events:

· Number Puzzle: Nonogram

· Articuline 1.0 - Advancements in IC Engines

· Core Session: Concorde

· Guess the Nutrient: Uncover the secrets behind your food!

· Little Scientists, Big Minds

· GeoRoot Quiz

· From Virtual to Real: Arduino Basics with Tinkercad

· SDG: CycleX

· Beyond the Spectrum–A talk on autism awareness

Scroll down for more details

VITMAS

Event Name: Number Puzzle: Nonogram

Event Time: 11:00 AM – 11:00 PM

Event Description: Decode hidden images through logical deduction and

number patterns! A fun way to boost your problem-solving abilities.

Venue: Google Forms (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/vitmas_?igsh=MWdnYWNkYXR4OTE0Yg==

AMERICAN SOCIETY OF MECHANICAL ENGINEERS

Event Name: Articuline 1.0 - Advancements in IC Engines

Event Time: 11:30 AM – 1:00 PM

Event Description: ARTICULINE 1.0 is a blog writing competition that

invites participants to explore and articulate their understanding of

modern engine technologies and the intricate components that drive today's

advanced automative systems. This event aims to foster technical writing

skills among students while deepening their knowledge.

Venue: Google Meet (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/asme.vit/

SOCIETY OF AUTOMOTIVE ENGINEERS

Event Name: Core Session: Concorde

Event Time: 7:30 PM – 8:30 PM

Event Description: Settle in your seats as we prepare to fly at twice the

speed of sound, because SAE-VIT airways bring you the CONCORDE. Back in the

60s flying at such supersonic speeds had technical hurdles which questioned

the very foundation of CONCORDE. But Britain and France had their own plans

to launch their Concorde program together. From being the 20th century’s

technically most ambitious project to having its economics shaken to the

ground, whether it will ever prove worthy. Was the Concorde project a

failure since its beginning?

Venue: Google Meet (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/sae_vit?igsh=dnJ2eG5pNWt4YnMz

Nutrition Club

Event Name: Guess the Nutrient

Uncover the secrets behind your food!

Event Time: 6:00 AM – 11:00 PM

Event Description: Put your nutrition knowledge to the test with Guess the

Nutrient! This fun, clue-based quiz by the Nutrition Club will challenge

you to identify essential vitamins, minerals, their food sources, and

deficiency diseases. Perfect for students, dietetics enthusiasts, and

trivia lovers.

Sharpen your knowledge, decode the clues, and Guess the Nutrient!

Venue: Google Forms (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/p/DIbW87WSWRZ/?igsh=dm1yZmUwamFzY3p6

Juvenile Care

Event Name: Little Scientists, Big Minds

Event Time: 2:00 PM – 5:00 PM

Event Description: An engaging science workshop where children will explore

fun, hands-on experiments designed to spark curiosity and foster a love for

learning.

Venue: St. Jude's Center

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link: https://www.instagram.com/juvenilecarevit/

LinkedIn Link: https://in.linkedin.com/company/juvenile-care-vit

Indian Geotechnical Society

Event Name: GeoRoot Quiz

Event Time: 9:00 AM – 9:00 PM

Event Description: GeoRoot Quiz by Indian Geotechnical Society is designed

to boost understanding of geotechnical concepts such as soil moisture

infiltration capillarity permeability water potential and plant water

dynamics The quiz is open to individual participants and includes time

bound multiple choice rounds that grow more challenging with each stage.

Venue: Google Forms (Online)

Registration: VTOP

Instagram Link:

https://www.instagram.com/igs.vit_?igsh=M251dm02cHAyd3N1&utm_source=qr

The Instrument Society of India

Event Name: From Virtual to Real: Arduino Basics with Tinkercad

Event Time: 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM

Event Description: Join us for an exciting hands-on workshop where you’ll

take your first steps into the world of Arduino and Tinkercad! Whether

you're a complete beginner or just looking to brush up on the basics, this

session will guide you through fundamental Arduino coding concepts, from

blinking an LED to reading sensor inputs. Then, we’ll dive into Tinkercad

Circuits, where you’ll simulate and test your Arduino projects in a virtual

environment—no hardware required! By the end of this workshop, you’ll have

the skills to design, code, and prototype simple circuits with confidence.

No prior experience needed—just bring your curiosity and get ready to bring

your ideas to life!

Venue: TT - 416

Well-being. This interactive session aims to raise awareness about the

importance of physical and mental health, preventive care, and healthy

lifestyle choices.

Venue: Dr. Ambedkar Auditorium, TT

subject: YANTRA'26: Day-9 Events (15-02-26) - Reg.
body:
Dear VITians,

As VIT continues its journey of excellence and innovation, the Office of

Students’ Welfare is proud to invite you to the 6th edition of Yantra —

VIT’s flagship week-long technical fest. Yantra’26, scheduled from 7th

February to 15th February 2026, promises an engaging and impactful

exploration of technology, creativity, and innovation.

This edition features 70+ diverse events, thoughtfully curated to

inspire, educate, and challenge participants across disciplines and skill

levels. The theme for Yantra’26, “Leveraging Web3 for Social

Responsibility”, highlights the transformative role of decentralization

and blockchain technology in fostering safe and transparent systems,

driving growth, enhancing societal well-being, and delivering sustainable

solutions to real-world challenges.

Visit our website for more details:

https://yantra.vit.ac.in/?utm_source=mail&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=yantra_mail

Don’t miss this opportunity to showcase your talent, strengthen your

technical skills, and collaborate on ideas that create meaningful impact.

Following are the events scheduled for YANTRA’26 – Day 9:

SPECIAL EVENT:

CENTRAL HACK

Date : 13-02-2026 to 15-02-2026

Time : 8 AM Onwards (56 hr hack - overnight)

Venue : ANNA AUDITORIUM

Event Details : The Yantra’26 is back with Central Hack, designed to bring

together the brightest minds, bold ideas, and passionate problem-solvers

from diverse academic backgrounds. With a prize pool of INR 6,00,000+,

Yantra Central Hack is a flagship 56-hour hackathon organized by the Office

of Students’ Welfare. The event brings together participants from multiple

disciplines to collaborate, innovate, and solve real-world challenges in an

intense, fast-paced environment.

PIXELATE CLUB

Event Name : Design Odyssey

Date : 14-02-2026 to 15-02-2026

Time : 8 AM to 8 PM

Venue : VOC GALLERY - TT

Event Details : Design Odyssey 2.0, hosted by Pixelate — the design club of

VIT — is a 36-hour intensive design sprint that challenges participants to

go beyond crypto hype and design for what truly matters: people, trust, and

social responsibility. While Web3 promises decentralization and

transparency, it often struggles with poor accessibility and complex

interfaces. Design Odyssey 2.0 invites creators to bridge this gap, using

design as the link between decentralized technology and real-world users.

Working within thematic tracks such as transparency, inclusivity, ethics,

sustainability, and privacy, teams will craft intuitive digital experiences

that make responsible choices simple and engaging — from transparent

donation platforms to ethical identity interfaces. This is not a coding

hackathon.

VIT MODEL UNITED NATIONS SOCIETY (VITMUN)

Event Name : MUNtra 2.0

Date : 14-02-2026 to 15-02-2026

Time : 9 AM to 5 PM

Venue : KAMARAJ AUDITORIUM - TT

Event Details :The MUN Society’s two-day workshop, explores how Web3

technologies are transforming global systems. Through structured debates

and role-based discussions, participants will examine topics such as data

ownership, digital sovereignty, cross-border payments, decentralised

identity, and governance of borderless platforms. The workshop progresses

from Web3 fundamentals to real-world geopolitical and social responsibility

challenges, encouraging critical analysis of how technology influences

global power structures and international cooperation.

AMERICAN SOCIETY OF MECHANICAL ENGINEERS (ASME)

Event Name : Speed Modelling Tournament

Date : 15-02-2026

Time : 8 AM to 6 PM

Venue : MB 210

Event Details :To identify the premier CAD designers who can translate

complex 2D engineering intent into high-fidelity 3D models and assemblies.

Success is measured by the proximity to a "Master Mass" and "Master Center

of Mass," with speed acting as the ultimate tie-breaker. Tests precision in

CAD modeling like real-life aerospace/automotive scenarios

subject: International Happiness Week (25th March 2026)-Day Four Event-Art therapy
body:
Dear VITians

Greetings from the Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being!

The Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being proudly brings you this week of

joy and happiness based on the theme, “Caring, Sharing and Well Being." Art

therapy provides a safe and creative outlet for students to express their

thoughts and feelings, especially when verbal communication may be

challenging. We are pleased to introduce Individual Art Therapy Sessions as

part of our ongoing efforts to support your mental health and emotional

well-being.

Art therapy is a guided, one-on-one process that uses creative

expression—such as drawing, painting, and visual exploration—to help you

understand and manage your thoughts and emotions. It is especially helpful

if you are experiencing stress, anxiety, academic pressure, or simply wish

to explore yourself in a safe and confidential space. No prior artistic

skill or experience is required.

Date: 25th March 2026

Venue: CS HALL (Venue changed from Era Sezhiyan Hall)

Time: 10.00 am to 01.00 pm

body: This email is being sent to zzzz@jmason.org. To unsubscribe please visit http://www.venturereporter.net/myaccount/ . If you ever have a problem removing or changing your email subscriptions on our newsletters, or getting in touch with us, please don't hesitate to email support@venturereporter.net and a human will get in touch with you immediately. Venture Reporter 307 West 36th Street, 10th Floor New York, New York 10018 Phoe: 646.473.2222 The online content business. http://www.cmsummit.com/images/right_02.gif http://www.cmsummit.com/images/cms_title.gif Dear Friends, The online content business is doing fantastic. Sound crazy? Perhaps. With advertising, online and off, taking it on the chin for the past two years, online content sites have been shutting down, laying off staff and pulling back on their offerings. However, this horrible environment has resulted in an undeniable trend: content businesses are challenging people to pay for content. Finally, after five years of free, people are beginning to understand that online, as in the real world, you get what you pay for and they are taking out their credit cards. U.S. consumers spent $675 million on paid online content last year, a 92 percent increase over 2000 spending levels, according to Online Publishers Association, and that figure is expected to increase exponentially this year. Look at these success stories: New York Times Digital has been steadily increasing its paid content services over the last year, and registered a 16 percent increase in its total revenues for the latest quarter. TheStreet.com brought over $3 million in subscriptions last quarter, an increase of almost 50 percent over the year-ago quarter. ConsumerReports.com will reach over a million paying subscribers by the end of this year. RealNetworks' consumer multi-media subscription service has more than 750,000 subscribers, bringing in $17.8 million in the last quarter. The Wall Street Journal Online added over 6,000 new paying customers last quarter, bringing its subscriber base to 646,000. FT.com has signed up 17,000 subscribers in three months since it launched its premium site in May. In recognition of this trend we're hosting the third installation of our innovative http://www.cmsummit.com Content Management Summit on October 10, 2002 . The event charts the changes in the content industry from free to paid subscription services, and the technologies that are enabling the management and monetizing of content. Our previous Content Management Summit (aka Digital Rights Summit) on October 18 last year in New York City and January 29 in Los Angeles were unqualified successes. The Content Management Summit III, taking place in New York at the Millennium Broadway on October 10, 2002, will bring together the 100 executives from the leading content and distribution firms for a focused day of networking and discovering practical solutions. The event will feature presentations from software and services companies providing services and solutions for selling, distributing, managing, and protecting content. We're thrilled that Microsoft, TeleKnowledge, eMeta, and Liquify will all be demonstrating their latest products and services. The event will also feature six intimate round tables focusing on various aspects of online content. These panels are meant to provide an informal forum to discuss the challenges facing these specific vertical markets, the changes in the sectors since the dot-com downfall, and best practices in the industry. The panels will feature leading practitioners in each sector, and will also include an interactive question and answer session with the audience. Among the round table topics will be: Weblogs: how they are affecting big media companies, editorially as well as in content delivery/production mechanisms. Financial news and information companies: how they are using technologies to deliver content to users, and how the economics have changed since the stock market downfall. Business information services such as Hoovers, Lexis-Nexis and others: best practices in the industry, niche product launches and revenue streams. Daily news/newspaper companies publishing online: how speed dictates technology choices, and the move towards paid content and its implications, among other issues. Consumer and entertainment publishers: how do publishers determine the value of entertainment content, the push towards paid subscriptions, online advertising and other issues. Join us on October 10 th for this very important event. If you are directly responsible for content management at a major content site you may qualify for a VIP ticket. Please e-mail your request with your name, title and bio to mailto:invite@cmsummit.com invite@cmsummit.com . If you are with a software or services provider, or anyone not directly responsible for the purchase of content management software or solutions, you can purchase a ticket to this event for $1,200 at mailto:invite@cmsummit.com invite@cmsummit.com . contributions.

We look forward to your enthusiastic participation and to celebrating the

spirit of engineering excellence together.

Dear students,

Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Science & Technology,

Government of India along with its Public Sector Undertaking, Biotechnology

Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) is organizing Global Bio-India

(GBI) 2023 from 4-6 December, 2023 at Bharat Mandapam & Hall no 14,

Pragati Maidan, New Delhi. The theme of the GBI-2023 is “Transforming

Lives-Biosciences to Bioeconomy”.

The event is expected to draw about 3000+ delegates from across the globe

connecting the Indian Biotechnology ecosystem with the International

ecosystem. This mega international congregation of biotechnology

stakeholders would include delegates from India and overseas representing

startups, SMEs, large companies, Central & State Ministries, research

organizations, incubators, investors, regulatory bodies, international

associations and other agencies.

BIRAC has decided to waive the Registration Fee for the event and there is

no restriction on the number of participants as well. For more details, see

the attached flyer. Further information on the event is available on GBI

website: https://www.globalbioindia.org

Dear VITians,

As part of the International Women’s Day Celebration, several engaging

events are scheduled today (10th March, 2026) for both faculty members and

students. The details are as follows:

 - Unlock Her Power – Escape Room Challenge

wit, and quick thinking as participants work together to solve clues and

challenges.

innovative and sustainable outfits, celebrating creativity and

environmental consciousness.

For Students :

 - Battle of the Boss Women – Designathon

ideas to life through creativity, design thinking, and problem-solving.

subject: Witness Innovation Unfold: Grand Finale of Yantra – Central Hack: Join Us Live!
body:
Dear VITians,

As we commemorate 40 years of excellence at VIT, the Office of Students'

Welfare invites you to the Grand Finale of Yantra – Central Hack, a

highlight of the weeklong tech fest, Yantra 2025. The Yantra Central Hack

has brought together brilliant minds to tackle real-world challenges, and

you’re invited to witness the magic unfold!

We have also invited esteemed dignitaries with specialized expertise to

judge the final review of the hack. (Details attached.)

The dignitaries include:

Dr. Prahlada Rama Rao – CEO and Co-founder of Hylenr Technologies

Dr. Jagandeep Singh Sidhu – Senior Product Engineer at CodeTantra

Dr. Shamneesh Sharma – Senior Manager, Program Delivery at UpGrad

Here’s your chance to be a part of the audience and experience the grand

finale of this incredible hackathon.

Event Details 

⏰ Audience Entry: February 9th, 5 PM onwards

📍 Venue: Era Sezhiyan Hall, Mahatma Gandhi Block

Why Join?

- Witness Innovation: Watch live problem-solving and cutting-edge solutions

in action.

- Gain Insights: Learn about emerging technologies and groundbreaking

ideas.

- Network: Interact with participants, mentors, and industry experts.

- Celebrate Excellence: Experience the final presentations and cheer for

the winners.

Don’t miss this exclusive opportunity to be inspired by transformative

ideas that are shaping the future.

See you there!

subject: Thanks message - Reg.
body:
Dear Students,

I hope you all truly enjoyed the DJ Night organized Yesterday and had a

memorable time. It was very encouraging to see your active participation,

positive energy, and enthusiasm throughout the event. I sincerely

appreciate each and every one of you for maintaining excellent discipline

and showing great cooperation, which played a key role in conducting the

program smoothly, safely, and without any hassles.

Such well-organized and joyful events are possible only when students

extend their wholehearted support and adhere to the guidelines provided.

Your responsible behavior reflects maturity and mutual respect, and it

makes organizing future activities more enjoyable and meaningful for

everyone involved.

We intend to organize many more cultural, recreational, and entertainment

programs for hostel students in the coming days, with the aim of creating a

lively, supportive, and welcoming environment where you can relax, connect

with one another, and truly feel a sense of belonging — a true “Home Away

From Home.”

We kindly request you to continue extending the same level of discipline,

cooperation, and enthusiasm for all future programs, so that we can

collectively ensure a positive and enriching hostel experience for everyone.

Once again, thank you all for your cooperation and for making Yesterday's

event a great success. We look forward to your continued support and

participation in the days ahead.

With Regards,

Prof. A. Sathiavelu,

body:

We are thrilled to share the incredible achievements of Team Kshatriya at

the recently concluded BAJA SAE INDIA 2025, one of the most prestigious

competitions in the field of automotive engineering and innovation.

Team Kshatriya delivered an exemplary performance, securing accolades in

multiple categories:

1st Place in Altair Simulation Awards: Excelling in the application of

cutting-edge simulation software to optimize vehicle design, safety, and

performance, earning them the top position in this highly technical segment.

2nd Place in Sled Pull: Demonstrating the strength and durability of

their ATV by towing a heavy sled across a challenging course with

remarkable efficiency and power.

These achievements underscore the team’s commitment to innovation,

technical expertise, and teamwork. Their success at BAJA SAE INDIA 2025 is

subject: The Room Cleaning Competition
body:
Dear Students,

Is your room a sanctuary of order or a chaotic "creative mess"? It's time

to settle the debate once and for all!

The Office of MH is officially launching The Room Cleaning Competition,

and we want to see which 3-to-6 bedded rooms have the best teamwork and the

sharpest organisational skills in MH.

This isn't just about tidying up--it's about transforming your living space

into the ultimate hostel suite. Grab your tools, gather your roommates, and

let the cleaning frenzy begin!

Event Details

 - Task: Record a time-lapse of your team deep-cleaning your room and

 snap those "Before & After" shots!

 - Contest Window: 5 April 2026 - 10 April 2026 (11:00 PM)

 - Eligibility: Exclusively for 3 to 6-bedded rooms.

The Top 2 Cleanest Rooms will be awarded with exciting prizes.

Rules to Remember

 1. Team Effort: Every single roommate must be seen pitching in during

 the time-lapse.

 2. Gear Up: Use your own cleaning supplies (no borrowing from

 maintenance!).

 3. Stay Original: No video editing allowed--we want to see the raw,

 real transformation.

 4. Keep it Legal: Ensure any prohibited items or property damage (no

 adhesives) are not part of your setup.

Ready to Scrub?

Show us your "After" photo that looks like your home! Submit your

time-lapse, photos, and the file details through the link given below.

For any queries, reach out to the Student Coordinator:

Sivanesh P - 9940296451

Submission Form Link: Click Here https://forms.gle/ntFn6xs48q2Zd1xs5

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [16th October] 

events.

World Food Day

The United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) marked October

16 of every year as World Food Day in the year 1979. In order to mark the

anniversary of the founding of the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO)

of the United Nations, every year, World Food Day is celebrated across the

globe on October 16. This day aims at tackling global hunger and striving

to eradicate hunger across the world. Every year, we celebrate World Food

Day to appreciate the amazing food we eat, but also to tackle world hunger.

Every year, the emphasis is on celebrating food heroes or individuals who

have contributed to building a sustainable world where no one has to go

hungry. The idea is that we all can be food heroes and contribute to the

idea of building a hunger-free world. FAO has also highlighted the work of

food heroes across the world who are working towards the same aspect. The

day is celebrated widely by many other organizations concerned with food

security, including the World Food Programme and the International Fund for

Agricultural Development.

subject: Summer Programme at Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) - Webinar
body:
Dear Students,

We are pleased to inform you that Queen Mary University of London (QMUL)

has received applications from several VIT students for their Summer

Programme.

To support interested applicants, QMUL has kindly offered to conduct an

online information webinar for our students.

🌍 Webinar Highlights

During the session, students will receive guidance on:

Overview of the QMUL Summer Programme

Application process and key deadlines

Required documents and eligibility

Tips for preparing a strong application

Opportunity to ask questions directly to QMUL representatives

📌 Who Should Attend?

This webinar is highly recommended for:

Students who have already applied

Students planning to apply soon

Anyone interested in international summer study opportunities

Supporting materials can be found on the website:

https://www.qmul.ac.uk/summer-school/

 Session Details

Date : 10th February (Today)

Time: 6.30 PM (IST)

Link:

https://events.teams.microsoft.com/event/840c9d46-2948-45b1-a897-0cbd424e0cc2@569df091-b013-40e3-86ee-bd9cb9e25814

Students are encouraged to participate actively and make the best use of

this opportunity.

subject: Congratulations to ASCE VIT for their Outstanding Performance at ASCE India Student Symposium 2026
body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that ASCE VIT delivered an exceptional

performance at the ASCE India Student Symposium 2026, organized by the

American Society of Civil Engineers – India Region, held from 23–30 March

2026 at Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh and the University of

Petroleum and Energy Studies (UPES), Dehradun.

The symposium witnessed participation from leading institutions across the

country, featuring a wide range of society-wide competitions and technical

events. Representing VIT, a team of 19 students demonstrated outstanding

technical expertise, teamwork, and innovation.

Achievements Secured:

Society-Wide Competitions:

UESI Surveying Competition – 1st Position

Sustainable Solutions Competition – 1st Position

Timber-Strong Design-Build Competition – 1st Position

Construction Institute Competition – 2nd Position

Paper Presentation – 2nd Position

Local Event:

Retro FitX – 1st Position

Team Members:

UESI Surveying Competition (1st Position):

 1. Abhinav Sahil Y – 23BCL0060

subject: Prima Vera'25 - Day-1 Events - reg
body:
Dear VITians,

Greetings!

The Office of Students' Welfare invites you to spring into action on Day-1

as we dive into an exciting week filled with cultural vibrance. After long

schedules and academic fatigue, this is the perfect moment to unwind,

recharge, and rediscover the joy of campus life.

We proudly present the 6th edition of Prima Vera - a week-long cultural

festival celebrating the creativity, passion, and spirit of VIT’s dynamic

student community. Get ready for a series of thrilling competitions, each

designed to bring out your best and help you showcase your unique talents.

Expect energetic performances, artistic showdowns, and engaging events, all

culminating in an unforgettable cultural experience.

And yes — there are exciting cash prizes waiting for the winners, along

with the pride of taking center stage in one of VIT’s most anticipated

festivals.

Gear up, participate, cheer, and make Prima Vera’25 a celebration to

remember!

Day-1 Schedule

Eshi no Sekai – Anime Drawing Competition is a highlight of PRIMA

VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their creativity and passion for

anime art. This competition provides a platform for new students to express

their imagination, experiment with styles, and demonstrate their drawing

skills in a supportive and inspiring environment. It aims to encourage

budding artists to step forward, celebrate their talent.

Kalligraphia – Calligraphy Competition (Solo Event) is one of the

signature contests of PRIMA VERA’25, designed to encourage freshers to

explore the elegance and discipline of artistic lettering. The competition

invites new students to express creativity through strokes, curves, and

handcrafted scripts, giving them a platform to showcase their precision,

style, and imagination. It aims to nurture emerging talent and help

freshers discover the beauty of calligraphy.

Rekha Kalā – Pencil Sketching Competition is an engaging contest under

PRIMA VERA’25, created to inspire freshers to explore the art of sketching

through lines, shades, and imagination. This competition encourages new

students to express their creativity using the simplicity of a pencil,

showcasing their ability to capture ideas, emotions, and forms with

precision. It serves as a platform for budding artists to discover their

potential, refine their skills.

Lux et Imago – DSLR Photography Competition is an exciting feature of

PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to step behind the lens and capture the

world through their unique perspective. This competition encourages new

students to explore light, composition, and storytelling through

photography, allowing them to express creativity and emotion in every

frame. It serves as a platform for budding photographers to showcase their

talent, experiment with techniques, and become part of VIT’s dynamic and

artistic community.

 Pixel Tales – Mobile Photography Competition is a vibrant and inclusive

contest under PRIMA VERA’25, encouraging freshers to capture creative

stories using nothing more than their mobile phones. This event empowers

new students to explore framing, lighting, and spontaneous moments, proving

that great photography doesn’t require professional gear—just vision and

imagination. It serves as an inviting platform for budding photographers to

showcase their perspective, experiment with mobile techniques.

 Swar Saaz – Solo Vocal (Eastern) Competition is a distinguished musical

event under PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their talent in

classical and semi-classical Eastern vocal music. This competition

encourages new students to express their voice, emotion, and artistry

through traditional melodies, offering them a stage to perform with

confidence and grace. It aims to nurture budding singers, celebrate the

richness of Eastern music, and welcome freshers into VIT’s vibrant cultural

and performing arts community.

 Vocal Virtuoso – Solo Vocal (Western) Competition is an electrifying

musical highlight of PRIMA VERA’25, inviting freshers to showcase their

talent in Western singing styles. This event encourages new students to

explore genres such as pop, rock, jazz, soul, and contemporary music,

giving them the space to express individuality, stage presence, and vocal

range. It provides a platform for budding performers to shine, build

confidence, and become part of VIT’s dynamic and diverse performing arts

community.

Get ready to shine at the 6th edition of Prima Vera — our annual cultural

extravaganza packed with creativity, energy, and endless fun. This year’s

edition brings together a vibrant lineup of competitions, performances, and

showcases designed to highlight the incredible talents of our students.

subject: Invitation to Participate – HACK IITK 2026 | IIT Kanpur
body:
Dear VITians,

The Association of Indian Universities (AIU) invites students to

participate in HACK IITK 2026, a national-level Hackathon organized by IIT

Kanpur’s C3iHub, India’s leading cybersecurity innovation hub.

The event aims to nurture young talent and promote innovation by

addressing real-world

cybersecurity challenges. It offers students and researchers a chance to

engage with industry experts, showcase their skills, and contribute to

solving critical cybersecurity issues.

Hackathon Tracks:

 - CTF (Capture the Flag) – focused on problem-solving and security

 skills

 - Solution Track – focused on developing practical solutions to

subject: Invitation: Foreign Expert Guest Lecture on "Influence in Science: how to win others' attention and be successful" by Dr. Manuel Mazzara (30th October 2025)
body:
Dear Faculty Members and Students,

We cordially invite you to a special Foreign Expert Guest Lecture organized

by the Sponsored Research and Industrial Consultancy (SpoRIC) and

TIFAC-CORE. This is a unique opportunity to gain strategic insights from

a distinguished international expert on how to maximize the visibility and

impact of your academic work.

Event Details

Topic:

"Influence in Science: how to win others' attention and be successful"

Speaker

: Dr. Manuel Mazzara (Professor of Computer Science & Dean of

Innopolis University, Kazan, Russia)

Date: 

Thursday, 30th October 2025

Time:

10:30 AM – 12:00 PM (IST)

Venue:

TT 707

About the Speaker: Dr. Mazzara is a Professor of Computer Science and the

Dean of the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering at Innopolis

University. With a Ph.D. from the University of Bologna and a career that

includes roles at Newcastle University and Microsoft, his expertise spans

software engineering, formal methods, and concurrency theory.

This lecture moves beyond technical research to focus on the essential

skills for career success: communicating impact, attracting collaborators,

and effectively positioning your work within the global scientific

community. All faculty members, research scholars, and students are

encouraged to attend. We look forward to your participation in this

insightful session. Invitation is attached herewith.

With high Regards,

Dr Suprava Chakraborty

Associate Professor & Deputy Director - TIFAC-CORE

subject: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program 2025-2026 (up to $60,000) – Opportunity Desk
body:
Dear VITians,

NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program 2024 – 2025

The application deadline for the 2024-2025 academic year is Sept. 7, 2023

NVIDIA Since its founding in 1993, NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) has been a pioneer

in accelerated computing. The company’s invention of the GPU in 1999

sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined computer graphics,

ignited the era of modern AI and is fueling the creation of the metaverse.

NVIDIA is now a full-stack computing company with data-center-scale

offerings that are reshaping industry.

This is the twenty-third year that NVIDIA has invited PhD students to

submit their research projects for consideration. Recipients are selected

based on their academic achievements, professor nomination, and area of

research. We have found this program to be a great way to support academia

in its pursuit of cutting edge innovation, as well as an ideal avenue to

introduce NVIDIA to the future leaders of our industry.

It focuses on supporting students working in AI, machine learning,

autonomous vehicles, computer graphics, robotics, healthcare, high

performance computing and related fields. Awards are up to $60,000 per

student.

NVIDIA has long believed that investing in university talent is beneficial

to the industry and key to our continued growth and success. The NVIDIA

Graduate Fellowship Program provides funding in the amount of up to $60,000

per award to PhD students who are researching topics that will lead to

major advances in accelerated computing and its applications. NVIDIA

particularly invites submissions from students pushing the envelope in

artificial intelligence, robotics, autonomous vehicles, and related fields.

We select students each year who have the talent, aptitude and initiative

to work closely with us early in their careers. Recipients not only receive

crucial funding for their research, but are able to conduct groundbreaking

work with access to NVIDIA products, technology and some of the most

talented minds in the field. In addition, the Fellowship includes a summer

internship preceding the Fellowship year.

NVIDIA partners with industry leaders to tackle some of the most complex

computing challenges. We’re creating profound change in fields as diverse

as medicine, space exploration, automotive design and film production.

We’ve only scratched the surface of what we can accomplish when we apply

our technology to it. We need innovative and talented doctoral students,

who aren’t afraid of a challenge, to help us tackle these opportunities.

Applications for 2024 are now open

Application

Eligibility

Students must have already completed their first year of PhD level studies

(at the time of application)

Students must have majors in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, System

Architecture, Electrical Engineering, or a related area

Students must be engaged in active research as part of their PhD thesis

Students must be enrolled as a full time active PhD student during the

2024-2025 academic year (9 months) of the award – this means they should

not be expecting to graduate sooner than May/June 2025.

Students must be available to complete a summer internship (which due to

COVID-19 may be held remotely) prior to the start of their Fellowship year.

Students may not be immediate family of a current NVIDIA employee

Note: The award must be administered through the student’s university;

payment will be made to the university, not directly to the student

Evaluation criteria

Proposals Will be Evaluated for:

Student quality

Letters of recommendation

Academic performance (GPA) and achievements

Research quality

Research results to date

Research proposal for fellowship

Publication track record

Relevance to NVIDIA

How your work connects to NVIDIA’s primary research domains

How your research might influence the design, performance or use of future

GPUs

Application instructions

Graduate Fellowship Applications Must Include:

Research summary/thesis proposal – up to 2 pages, plus bibliography

(bibliography does not count toward 2 page maximum for proposal)

Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV) including contact information

Professor nomination letters (2 letters minimum (must include one from

thesis advisor), up to 3 letters maximum — OK to have nomination letters

from non-professors, as long as you have one from your thesis

advisor/professor).

Confirmation of availability for summer internship

Submission Portal: It is the student’s responsibility to ensure that all of

these items are submitted prior to the deadline. We are using a Submission

Portal in which the student manages their own application. The student must:

Complete the student profile – start this now; you can go back to the

portal repeatedly until you submit the final application

Complete your application input including research summary thesis proposal

and resume (CV)

Add contacts for the letters of recommendation — an email will

automatically be sent on your behalf to each recommender you add — be sure

to add your professors/recommenders early in the process! Do not wait until

close to the deadline!

Monitor the status of your recommendation letters in the portal — do not

click on the final submission until the recommendation status shows

“recommendation uploaded” for each recommendation you are expecting — the

professor deadline has been set 1 day prior to the student deadline to

allow the student to ensure all documents are received before submitting —

the deadline for recommendation letters is 3pm Pacific September 6, 2023.

Communicate with the recommenders to complete their letter upload on time –

it is the student’s responsibility to ensure their letters are received

into the system.

Submit the final application when all items are complete, and prior to the

application deadline: 3pm Pacific September 7, 2023.

Submissions are currently OPEN. Please access the submission site here.

Notifications of final decisions will be emailed by the end of November

Terms and Conditions

The Graduate Fellowship Award must be used to further your research. The

breakdown of the award is between stipend, tuition and health insurance, in

that order. The award is an unrestricted gift to be used to further the

student’s research over the academic year. We ask that no overhead or

indirect costs are charged to the award. Awards are not transferable to

another student. Whether it is OK to combine the NVIDIA fellowship with

another fellowship depends on several factors — please contact the NVIDIA

Graduate Fellowship for details on this matter. Awards are issued to the

university for disbursement, not directly to the student. Amount of the

award cannot exceed stipend, tuition, and health insurance. There may also

be university-specific restrictions that pertain. Applications include

permission to use the student’s submission data for evaluation of a

potential fellowship award. Applicants may choose to opt-in for an

internship evaluation outside of the fellowship (in the event the applicant

is not chosen for an award.) If selected for an award, a completed

internship at NVIDIA is required before the Fellowship award year can

begin. Immediate family of NVIDIA employees cannot participate.

Helpful Hints for the Graduate Fellowship Submission: The Recommendation

Letter

A heavily-weighted component of the application evaluation is the

recommendation letter. It is therefore recommended that the candidate

afford it the proper attention and effort; here are a few tips that we

suggest:

Pick your recommenders wisely!

Your thesis advisor is required, but beyond that, you should select only

people who know you well enough to write a strong recommendation for you. A

recommendation from a high-profile researcher who barely knows you, or has

not worked with you, does not help your application.

Ask each of your recommenders in person/via email before you send the

request from the NVIDIA Grad Fellow portal. Ask them also if they have time

to write such a letter by the due date. If they are traveling or focused on

another deadline, their letter may be hastily composed and not help your

cause. It is also generally OK to ask them directly if they feel

comfortable writing a strong recommendation letter. If this is someone you

only took a class from a few semesters ago, they might not remember you

well enough to write you the kind of recommendation you are seeking – give

them a chance to tell you. If that is the case, then thank them and move on

to asking someone who knows you better.

If you are asking a recommender in industry, such as a former boss from a

summer internship, you may need to remind them what you’ve been working on

since they last worked with you. It always helps if you can stay in

somewhat regular touch with such contacts, so that a lot of time doesn’t

pass between updates.

Provide your recommenders with sufficient notice.

Your recommenders are busy people and cannot always pull off a last-minute

request. Give them at least a 2 week notice if possible.

Be sure to send the request from the submission portal early and

double-check with them that they received the email from the system –

sometimes the email goes into their spam folder, and it’s harder to find

when it’s the day before the deadline. Ask them to please confirm receipt

of the email within 24 hours of your sending it from the portal.

Send them a couple of polite reminders: if you’ve given them 2 weeks,

perhaps send a reminder at the one-week mark, and if they still haven’t

submitted the letter 3 days prior to the deadline (remember, you can check

their letter status on the submission portal), then send them one more

reminder.

Thank them for their recommendation as soon as you see their letter has

been submitted!

Graduate Fellowships FAQs

Do you have a specific research field requirement in EE, CE, or CS?

No. There are many ways that Engineering fields can touch NVIDIA, and we

are open to considering them.

 I am just starting my PhD this Fall. Am I eligible to apply?

You should have completed your first year of your PhD program at the time

of application. The requirement is not black and white, but the idea is

that after one year, there is a track record of research and experience.

With no Ph.D. experience, there is very little to judge the student’s

research on. So, it’s certainly fine to apply, but very unlikely to be

awarded. Of course, in special situations, there may be enough history to

make a compelling application. We suggest you look at the list of past

recipients and see whether your application is comparable. If so, then go

ahead and apply and see where your application falls in the review process

compared to all the other applications.

Do I need to have accepted publications?

Our prior fellowship recipients have had track records of multiple

publications in top-tier venues of their fields. To be competitive, you

should have at least one strong publication.

Is there a limit on how many Graduate Fellowship Awards one PhD student can

receive from NVIDIA?

No. At this time there is no limit on the number of times you can be

awarded the NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Award. Keep in mind you can only

receive one per year!

Is there a limit to the number of NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Awards granted

per University or per Research Team?

No. At this time, there is no limit per University nor is there a limit per

graduate team provided the research is different and interesting to NVIDIA.

I am a current Graduate Fellowship Recipient, can I apply again?

Yes. You can apply each year you are enrolled full-time until the year

before you complete your PhD. You can follow the same guidelines and

application process as any new applicant.

Are International PhD students eligible?

Yes. International students are eligible to apply. Keep in mind, the

Graduate Fellowship Award amount may vary by country, region or location.

Can I have more than one Professor Nomination Letter?

Yes, you can have up to three Professor Nomination Letters. It is OK to

have nomination letter(s) from non-professors, as long as you have one from

your thesis advisor/professor.

What if my professor/advisor doesn’t submit the Professor Nomination Letter?

We do require at least one Professor Nomination Letter from your thesis

advisor. Please be sure to add your recommendation contacts into the portal

early in the process so that your professor(s) have sufficient notice and

time to compose and upload their letter. Please remember it is the

student’s responsibility to ensure the professor nominations are turned in

on time, and following up with them prior to the deadline if they haven’t

uploaded their letter into the portal.

How are the Graduate Fellowship Recipients selected?

NVIDIA’s Graduate Fellowship Program has a committee of engineers headed by

our Chief Scientist, Bill Dally. The committee is comprised of over 60

senior technical staff and managers from research and development groups

across the company. This committee reviews all applicants competitively in

several review sessions. This is a very intensive process. The entire

review process usually takes about 8 weeks. Unfortunately, many qualified

candidates will not be selected due to the high quality of proposals and

limited number of awards available.

Can I work a part-time job during my Fellowship?

The goal of covering your stipend in full is to release you from the need

to work as a TA/RA or another outside job, and allow you to focus on your

research. However, we realize that sometimes part-time jobs provide a

benefit to the student other than money, and in those cases as long as the

work is beneficial to the progress of your PhD and a conflict of interest

does not exist between NVIDIA and the other entity, this would be

acceptable to NVIDIA. If there is any doubt on the conflict of interest,

please check with your NVIDIA Fellowship contact.

Click here to know more and apply

https://opportunitydesk.org/2024/08/23/nvidia-graduate-fellowship-program-2025-2026/

Thanks and Regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

body:
Dear Student,

Guidelines – Course Registration (Fall Semester 2026 - 27)

 1. Senior Students and timed-out students of all the programmes except

 BSc (Agri), BSc Catering & Hotel Management, B. Des., B. Arc., BSc

 Multimedia, BSc Visual Communication, M. Des., M. Arc., MSW, B. Tech

 Computer Science and Business Systems (2023 & 2024 Batch) are permitted

 to take part in the course registration.

 2. Course Registration is scheduled to be conducted on 28. 06. 2026.

 3. Information on the course registration schedule for the Fall Semester

 2026 - 27 (time and duration for various groups of students) will be made

 available on VTOP and the VITian Mobile App on 25th June 2026.

 4. Information on courses offered for the Fall Semester 2026 - 27 will

 be made available on VTOP and the VITian Mobile App on 26th June 2026

 5. During the course registration process (on 28.06.2026), all the core,

 elective and compulsory courses with the following options will be

 permitted:

 Regular / Re-register / Substitution (UE / OE / DE / PE and

also in HSM / Language Basket)

 Regular (UC as UE, PE as UE, DE as OE, SPE as OE)

 Minor / Honour / Second Major Programmes

Multidisciplinary Elective (applicable to the 2023 & 2024 Batch B. Tech

Core Programmes only, except BBS): An option is provided to earn the

required credits under the Discipline Elective / Open Elective category by

registering courses listed under multidisciplinary electives. The

eligibility criteria to register for course(s) under the multidisciplinary

elective are to have completed a minimum of 9 credits from the courses

listed under the Discipline Electives. The remaining credits can be earned

from courses listed under either Discipline Electives or Multidisciplinary

Electives to meet the credit requirements as per the curriculum.

 6. The add / Drop option will be enabled for all the students from

 06.07.26 to 08.07.2026. During the Add / Drop period, students can register

 for courses under Audit / Grade Improvement / Additional Course / Minor /

 Honour / Second Major options.

 7. Removal of courses registered under the regular mode is not possible

 unless the course registered under ‘Additional’ is removed first.

 8. The student should generate an invoice on VTOP (in the timetable

 menu) and proceed for payment (under the menu – Online Payments) for the

 courses that demand course fees. The courses of fee defaulters will be

 deregistered after the deadline.

 9. Courses cannot be deleted or withdrawn if the fee payment is made.

 10. Students are required to go through the Academic Regulations for

 further clarification on the terminology.

 11. Queries related to course offerings should be addressed to the

 respective Head of the Department.

Project Registration Rules 

All eligible M. Tech./ MCA /MSc students who were admitted in 2025

-26 will be permitted to register for Internship I/ Dissertation I during

the Fall Semester 2026-27 with a duration of 6 months.

Integrated students of MIC/MID/MIY who are admitted in 2022-23 will be

permitted to register for the Capstone project/Master's thesis with a

duration of 12 months.

BXXX497J - Project I is compulsory for the 2023-24 batch B.Tech. students.

During registration, students should select a guide and a tentative project

title.

BAXXX291 – Innovative Design Project is compulsory for the 2025-26 batch

B.Tech students. During registration, students should select a guide and a

tentative project title.

Kindly note that there will be two options to register for Internship I /

Dissertation I / Capstone Project / Master Thesis:

a) ACAD - ACADEMICS

b) PAT - PLACEMENT AND TRAINING

Students who have already received an Internship offer through CDC have to

register for the course under “PAT - PLACEMENT AND TRAINING”. The remaining

students have to register under ACAD – Academics, for which a “Faculty

Guide” is to be selected. (Guide change option will be enabled during the

Add / Drop period)

Students can change the option from ACAD to PAT whenever an internship

offer is received in future by submitting proof (received from the CDC) and

a consent letter (from the Guide) to the Academics Office.

with regards

M. Anthony Xavior PhD

Dean Academics

subject: Undergraduate (UG) Research publications and Achievements for April 2026
body:
Dear Students,

Warm greetings from the UG Research Cell !!

We are pleased to share the Undergraduate (UG) Research Achievements for

April 2026. Our UG students have demonstrated excellent involvement in

research and innovation through their contributions to journal

publications, conference papers, and patent filings. These achievements

reflect their strong commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and

research.

A total of 160 students from various disciplines contributed to research

publications, resulting in 75 publications during this period.

Furthermore, the active involvement of 110 students in research and

innovation initiatives resulted in the filing of 53 patents during April

2026.

 

 

 

 

We sincerely congratulate all the students for their efforts and

achievements. Your hard work, dedication, and research interests are truly

appreciated.

This update is not only to recognize your success, but also to encourage

other UG students to get involved in research. If your peers can do it, you

can too. There are plenty of research opportunities available for students

from all branches and years.

Thank You.

Yours Sincerely,

C. Rajasekaran

subject: INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR WINTER 2023-24 THEORY FAT
body:
Dear Students 

Please read the following instructions carefully:

INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR WINTER

 2023-24 THEORY FAT

Students appearing for FAT Exams, please READ INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY TILL

the END.

1. As per new regulations, the students must enter the examination hall

15-30 Minutes before the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15

AM for FN Session). Students reporting beyond the specified entry time will

not be permitted to enter the examination hall. 

2. Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

3. Students are not permitted to take the following materials inside the

exam halls: chit papers, mobile phones, ear buds, the lid of the

calculator, chit materials, a reference table that contains markings,

written content using pencil or pen, nano ear phones, electronic devices,

blue tooth devices/displays, mobile phones without SIM cards,

non-transparent pouches, microxeroxes, or any other irrelevant material to

the exams. Possession itself and/or its use of any of the above is

considered examination malpractice.

4. Malpractice rules are published in the student VTOP login; you are

required to go through them, and you are requested not to indulge in any

examination malpractices.

3. Based on the requirements, Frisking will be done prior to entering the

examination hall and during the examination. You may be required to do

self-frisking before entering into examination hall. Also two to five

minutes are permitted to do the same inside the exam hall before collecting

question paper and answer booklet.

4. If a student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she has to

submit the question paper along with answer sheet. 

5. On the day of exam, keep your bags in front of exam room, DONOT TAKE

NOTE BOOKS / BOOKS / BAGS TO EXAM DESKS

General Instructions

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE EXAMINATION

PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact Registrar Office and

apply for a new one and get it before coming to the Exam. The ID card

should be scratches free with proper tag. Exchange of ID cards or Tags will

be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced your ID card or forgot

to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the Control Room of your

test venue to get One Time Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through

V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationaries, Code Books, pen, pencil etc.,

are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either by the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep mobile phone/smart watch in a

switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated as

examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of the

devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phone/smart watch

by mistake.

A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to exam. No student would be permitted to enter the hall

after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of un-authorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you in

the floor and inform the same to the invigilators.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any thin pens, / light colours may not be visible on

the scanned images used for evaluation. Remember to write the answers

within the space provided in the answer booklet. If you write anything

outside the margin, it will be cut during the scanning process. If you are

using extra sheets like graph sheets / templates given by faculty, write

your registration number alone on top left edge outside the margin and keep

it immediately after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it needs to be

scanned for valuation. Do your rough works in the last page of main answer

booklet itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all the rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg ot on

desk or on walls nearby you.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask question of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by invigilator. You

cannot leave the examinations hall till 30 min from the start of the

examination.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused one, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets, no threads,

will be provided. 

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the exam squad / Invigilator / Asst. CS / CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

/ diverting attention of all other students, a scene in the examination

hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

4.

Examination malpractice actions/punishments are very serious, may lead to

All paper ZERO or suspension of one semester. All are malpractice actions

are informed to the students / published in VTOP student Login. Please go

through it follow the examination rules appropriately

5.

body: Allexecs.org Greetings! If you're thinking about a new job, now's the time to aggressively pick up your search. Many people slow their job search donw in summer months when in fact it's the best time to look! Here's why. Many companies implement a new direction or strategy at the first of the year, resulting in a first of the year hiring surge. By mid year, with results in hand, companies start hiring again to expand on or adjust for the results of their first of the year plans. While employers start hiring, job seekers start slowing their search efforts down. This creates an optimal job seeking environment of more jobs and less competition! To best take advantage of this situation you should give yourself massive exposure by signing up to all the top career sites as soon as possible. Of course it will take a little time, but it's well worth it. The top career sites are visited by 1.5 million employers and recruiters daily - And collectively list millions of jobs. If you want to save 60 hours of research and data entry, try a service called ResumeRabbit.com. They instantly post your resume to 75 the top career sites at once. You'll find this service at http://start.resumerabbit.com With this service you fill out one simple form in about 15 minutes and you'll be instantly seen on Monster.com, HotJobs.com, Job.com CareerBuilder.com, Dice.com and more! When searching for a new job, it's important to work smart and cover a lot of ground. Today's serious job seeker must take a multi-pronged approach to succeed. This should include networking, reading all the classifieds, posting your resume on all the top career sites and searching job listings on these sites daily. We recommend you try http://start.resumerabbit.com It's a quality service that delivers what it promises. >>From mid November to mid January, the holidays have a "slowing down" effect on hiring. Since the job search process can often be several months, waiting until the end of summer to get started may push your new job off well after the new year. Now's the optimum time to aggressively mount your search! Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [17th October] 

events.

International Day for the Eradication of Poverty

The UN general assembly declared 17 October as the International Day for

the Eradication of Poverty and invited all States to devote the Day to

presenting and promoting, as appropriate in the national context, concrete

activities with regard to the eradication of poverty and destitution.

October 17th presents an opportunity to acknowledge the effort and struggle

of people living in poverty, a chance for them to make their concerns

heard, and a moment to recognize that poor people are the first ones to

fight against poverty. The participation of the poor themselves has been at

the center of the Day’s celebration since its very beginning. The

commemoration of October 17th also reflects the willingness of people

living in poverty to use their expertise to contribute to the eradication

of poverty.

development. We'll cover Swift basics, introduce SwiftUI for UI design, and

layouts, manage state, and implement data persistence. By the end, you'll

constellations, and other astronomical phenomena in the comment section.

subject: Fwd: Exciting opportunity to Join Team Lambda – Drive Innovation in Robotics, AI, and Smart Systems
body:
Dear Students,

Greetings from Team Lambda!

We are pleased to announce that Team Lambda, an official SELECT team

from VIT

Vellore, is now recruiting passionate and skilled individuals across

departments for cutting‑edge projects. This is an opportunity for

passionate students to contribute to industrial research, real‑time

product development, and international collaborations—and gain

experience through funded Government of India initiatives.

About Team Lambda

Team Lambda is a multidisciplinary research and product‑development team

working on:

 -

 Autonomous Robot Development

 -

 Predictive Solar Panel Maintenance

 -

 Smart Infrastructure and Digital Twin Systems

Our projects are funded by the Department of Science and Technology (DST),

Government of India, and partner industries.

Highlights and Achievements

 -

 Winners of Innovation Week 2025, VIT’s flagship competition for

 technological innovation

 -

 Represented VIT at IInventive 2025 (IIT Madras) for showcasing

 autonomous bots and smart energy systems

 -

 Engaged in collaborative research with leading institutes and

 industrial organizations

Connect with us on LinkedIn using

Team Lambda – VIT Vellore

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.linkedin.com/company/team-lambda-vit&source=gmail-imap&ust=1748195611000000&usg=AOvVaw0P8bnGFhxoWPFx_fk1RlUK

Why Join Team Lambda?

 -

 Work on fully funded government and industry‑backed projects

 -

 No membership fee is charged

 -

 Internship Completion Certificate will be provided

 -

 Opportunity for long‑term core membership based on performance

 -

 Project work presented at national‑level tech fests

 -

 Enhance your technical, research, and leadership capabilities

Top‑performing interns will be considered for core positions within Team

Lambda.

Application Details

Apply here: https://forms.gle/r13MkPPqfeuXpMAp6

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://forms.gle/r13MkPPqfeuXpMAp6&source=gmail-imap&ust=1748195611000000&usg=AOvVaw177KU-y3n5_MVdSriaHYvh

Application Deadline: 26th May 2025, 9:00 PM

Domains Open for Recruitment Computer Science:

Frontend Developer

 -

 Proficiency in React.js, JavaScript, and HTML/CSS

 -

 Experience in building responsive and modular UI components

App Developer

 -

 Proficiency in React Native or Flutter

 -

 Experience with RESTful APIs and backend integration

AI and ML Developer

 -

 Proficiency in Python with frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch

 -

 Experience with CNNs, RNNs, and classical machine learning techniques

 -

 Familiarity with OpenCV, Flask, scikit‑learn, NumPy, and Pandas is

 preferred

Electrical / Electronics / Instrumentation (EEE / EIE / ECE):

PCB Designing

 -

 Previous experience designing PCBs in KiCAD

Analog Design

 -

 Component selection and analog circuit design for signal processing

Motor Drive Integration

 -

 Proficiency in BLDC motor integration with drivers (e.g., BLD‑120A)

 -

 Hands‑on with PWM, I2C, SPI protocols and real‑time control

 -

 Tools: MATLAB/Simulink, Proteus, Multisim, LTspice, PSpice

Power Supply and Battery Management (BMS)

 -

 BMS design and management for Li‑ion and similar chemistries

 -

 DC‑DC converters, voltage regulation, and power‑system design

 -

 Tools: Altium Designer, KiCad, Eagle, MATLAB, LTspice

Sensor Integration and Electronics

 -

 Integration and calibration of IR, ultrasonic, gyroscope, and other

 sensors

 -

 ADC/DAC conversion and signal‑conditioning techniques

Embedded Systems and Automation

 -

 Programming in Embedded C, Python, and C++

 -

 Hardware‑software interfacing on microcontrollers and single‑board

 computers

 -

 Familiarity with Raspberry Pi, UART, SPI, CAN bus, and IoT platforms

Mechanical Engineering:

CAD/CAM/CAE

 -

 SolidWorks, Fusion 360, AutoCAD, and Ansys for design and simulation

Stress and Vibration Analysis

 -

 Static and dynamic analysis in ANSYS

 -

 Vibration‑mode identification using DADiSP

Robotic Mechanisms and Kinematics

 -

 Simulation with Webots or similar tools

 -

 Kinematics, dynamics, and motion planning for robotic arms and bots

Manufacturing and Prototyping

 -

 3D printing, manual tools, and rapid prototyping techniques

 -

 Material selection for efficiency and durability

Mechanical Systems and Hands‑on Skills

 -

 Understanding of suspensions and actuator technologies

 -

 Practical experience with machine tools and mechanical assemblies

Marketing and Finance:

 -

 Conduct market surveys and analyze industry trends

 -

 Manage project budgeting and financial planning

 -

 Develop business models and go‑to‑market strategies

Students from VIT Business School are encouraged to apply.

Join us to become part of a high‑performance, interdisciplinary team

passionate about building technology that matters. We are committed to

mentorship, national recognition, and real‑world innovation.

We look forward to having you onboard.

Warm regards,

Team Lambda

Follow us on LinkedIn

https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.linkedin.com/company/team-lambda-vit&source=gmail-imap&ust=1748195611000000&usg=AOvVaw0P8bnGFhxoWPFx_fk1RlUK

Thanks and regards,

Dr.N.Rajasekar,

subject: Deep Tech Research Program-Empowering Breakthrough Innovations_
body:
Dear Students, Research Scholars and Professors,

Greetings,

 VIT takes great effort in promoting the Deep Tech Research Program as an

initiative to foster cutting-edge research and innovation in transformative

technologies through Chancellor's Fellowship.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between academia and industry, driving

societal impact through scientific advancements.

Research Focus Areas

• Artificial Intelligence/Generative AI

(Healthcare/Climate/Environment/Energy/Finance)

• Machine Learning/Deep Learning

• Wireless Networks/IOT

• Image and Vision Computing

• Autonomous Robot

• Quantum Computing

• Cyber Security

• Space Technologies

• Blockchain Technologies

• Precision Agriculture

• Sustainable development

• Biotechnology (Genomics/Synthetic Biology/Food production/Fuel)

• Any other areas mentioned by NITI Ayog

(Problem Statement proposed by Research Scholar With the faculty guide

acting as mentorship) - Outcome Product Development –TRL 6

Eligibility:

Graduates must have an outstanding academic record in their Bachelor’s

Degree in Engineering / Technology are eligible to apply. A minimum of 75%

marks or a CGPA of 7.5 is mandatory on a 10- point scale or Master’s

degree in Engineering / Technology in the relevant discipline with a

minimum of 75% marks (of all the years /semesters) wherever marks are

awarded, or a CGPA 7.5 on a 10-point scale in cases where letter grades are

awarded or Equivalent qualifications like M.Sc. (Engineering) / M.S. [By

Research] / M.Tech. [By Research] in full-time or regular mode of

education is mandatory

Deep Tech Research Chancellor's Fellowship:

 First Year

• ₹ 40,000 (GATE Qualified (Above 60 Percentile)); 

• ₹ 35,000 (Others)

• 2nd- 3rd Years

• ₹50,000(GATE Qualified (Above 60 Percentile)); 

• ₹ 45,000 (Others)

Funding Extendable for 4th Year

 Periodic review of innovation, and patent attainment level will be

assessed.

 Tangible Outcome:

Product Development upto TRL6 is mandatory for getting 4th Year funding

support.

Apply now and join our community of innovative researchers

Kindly forward this mail to all your contacts and potential future

innovators.

Thanks and high regards

Yours Sincerely,

P.Arulmozhivarman

--------------------------------------------

Dr. P. Arulmozhivarman

Professor & Dean Academic Research

Vellore Institute of Technology

Vellore 632014, TN, India.

Parakram Diwas

Parakram Diwas (Bravery Day) is celebrated in India on 23 January. It was

introduced by the Government of India in 2021 to celebrate Netaji Subhas

Chandra Bose's 125th birth anniversary. Parakram Diwas will be celebrated

'in order to honor and remember Netaji's indomitable spirit and selfless

service to the nation'. Parakram Diwas is celebrated to inspire people of

this country, especially the youth, to act with fortitude in the face of

adversity as Netaji did, and to infuse in them a spirit of patriotic fervor.

Of the many freedom fighters who laid their lives for the country's cause,

Subhash Chandra Bose is one of those that is fondly remembered by the

Indians. Popularly known as 'Netaji', he was born on January 23, 1897. His

aim was simple: to get India the much-needed independence. Despite his

differences, it was the ultimate goal of freedom that did not deter him

from that path.

Bengali Literary Association (Aikyataan)

tribute to Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose through it's elocution contest,

his birth anniversary. Join us at the Ambedkar Auditorium on 23rd January,

2024 at 9am. Let the power of words resonate in celebration of Netaji's

Essay Writing Competition (Tamil)

Topic: Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh (திருவள்ளூவரின் தமிழ்)

Thiruvalluvar was a renowned Tamil poet-philosopher who is best known for

his work, the Thirukkural. He is considered one of the greatest Tamil poets

and his work is highly respected in Tamil culture. Thiruvalluvar's life and

times are not well-known, and there are many different accounts of his

life. However, it is generally believed that he lived sometime between the

3rd century BCE and the 5th century CE. He is said to have been born in

Mylapore, a suburb of present-day Chennai, India.

The Thirukkural is a collection of 1330 couplets that are divided into

three parts: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth), and Inbam (love). The text

covers a wide range of topics, including ethics, politics, economics, and

love. The Thirukkural is known for its wisdom and its insights into human

nature. It has been translated into many languages and is considered one of

the most important works of Tamil literature.

Despite Tiruvalluvar’s reasonable tone, many of his ideas were

revolutionary. He dismissed the caste system: “One is not great because of

one’s birth in a noble family; one is not low because of one’s low birth.”

The poet maintained that goodness is its own reward and should not be

regarded as a mere means to a comfortable afterlife.

Thiruvalluvar says that the only indestructible wealth is education. He

says a person who shuns learning is akin to an animal. Comparing those who

read with those who do not is not an appropriate comparison, for how can

one compare man and beast?

Calling all writers! Share your insights on "Thiruvalluvarin Tamizh" in a

500-word essay.

Scroll down for more details

World Kindness Day

World Kindness Day 2023 is a global observance dedicated to promoting and

celebrating acts of kindness. This day serves as a reminder of the positive

impact that kindness can have on individuals, communities, and the world at

large. It encourages people to perform intentional acts of kindness and

foster a culture of compassion and generosity.

The theme for the year 2023 is a powerful reminder – “Be Kind Wherever

Possible.” The theme for this year underscores the importance of kindness

as a universal principle that should be practiced in every corner of the

globe and in every aspect of our lives.

As part of World Kindness Day, CCs are doing 1 Event.

VIT LEO CLUB

Event Name: Kindness Quest

Time: 09:00 AM - 05:00 PM

Event Platform: Instagram

Event Description: World Kindness Day is celebrated every year on November

13th. This day was first introduced in a conference in Tokyo by the World

Kindness Movement, a coalition of NGOs from various countries across the

globe. This day serves as a global reminder to promote and celebrate acts

of kindness and encourage goodwill among individuals and communities, and

to demonstrate that even the smallest acts of kindness and empathy can

create far-reaching ripple effects of positivity out into the world. It's a

day when we unite across all borders to promote compassion, empathy, and

understanding. To celebrate this day, VIT Leo Club presents you with

"Kindness Quest", a quizzing event. In this quiz, we'll explore the

history, stories, and significance of kindness in our lives.

Join us on this enlightening journey, where each quiz question is a

International Day of the Girl Child

International Day of the Girl Child is an international observance day

declared by the United Nations, to recognize girls’ rights and the unique

challenges girls face around the world. The International Day of the Girl

Child focuses attention on the need to address the challenges girls face

and to promote girls’ empowerment and the fulfillment of their human rights.

The observation supports more opportunities for girls and increases

awareness of gender inequality faced by girls worldwide based upon their

gender. This inequality includes areas such as access to education,

nutrition, legal rights, medical care, and protection from discrimination,

violence against women, and forced child marriage. The celebration of the

day also "reflects the successful emergence of girls and young women as a

distinct cohort in development policy, programming, campaigning, and

research.

As part of the International Day of the Girl Child, CC are organising 4

events.

FEPSI

Time: 10:00AM

Event Platform: Google Forms

Event details: Join us in celebrating the power of creativity and

International Girl Child Day with our submission-based event "Her Canvas,

that champion the rights, equality, and dreams of every girl child. This

girl child through vibrant colors and powerful messages. Send us your

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [16th September]

International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer

International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer falls on

September 16 every year. The ozone layer around our planet is like our

favorite childhood blanket — safe, protective, and only requires a little

attention and care in return. International Day for the Preservation of the

Ozone Layer is a day dedicated to giving back to our planet, and more

specifically, the ozone layer.

To commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol, the United Nations

General Assembly declared September 16 as the International Day for the

Preservation of the Ozone Layer in 1994. Also known as World Ozone Day,

September 16 has since then been dedicated each year to the appreciation

and preservation of this protective layer and the success of the Vienna

Convention
