Kind Attention Undergraduate Students!

Ming Chi University of Technology, Taiwan has announced the start of the

recruitment process for the 2026 MCUT Language and Culture Summer Camp!

Objectives:

 1. To inspire participants to consider pursuing further education in

 Taiwan.

 2. To provide students with insights into the degree programs available

 at MCUT.

Camp Dates:

Session 1 (July): July 6 – July 15, 2026

Session 2 (August): August 10 – August 21, 2026

(Note: August 19–21 will feature a special cultural exchange with local

Taiwanese high school students)

Participation Highlights:

 1. Program Fee: 100% WAIVED. This includes course fees,

 accommodation, one to two meals per day, tour bus transportation (including

 airport transfers), local accident insurance, and cultural field trips.

 2. Student Expenses: Participants are responsible for their round-trip

 airfare, visa fees, and personal living expenses.

Nomination & Eligibility:

 1. Quota: Each partner university may nominate up to two (2) students

 .

 2. Undergraduate students from MCUT's overseas partner universities.

 3. Applicants' majors must be aligned with the degree programs offered

 at MCUT. Please verify the corresponding departments via our official

 website. https://www.mcut.edu.tw/p/412-1000-6888.php?Lang=en

 4. Language Requirement: Students should possess English proficiency

 equivalent to CEFR B1 or above.

 5. Restriction: Each student may participate in only one of the two

 sessions.

Application Process:

 1. How to Apply: To ensure effective coordination, we kindly request

 that faculty members or international office staff fill out the Online

 Registration Link https://forms.gle/auJPUMgNQpyThYyF6 on behalf of the

 accepted.

subject: Notice: Internship Career 2025- 3rd Year VIT Students!" (Apply Now Deadline Approaching)
body:
Dear VIT Student,

We are excited to announce a unique, Skill and Startup India-approved

3-month Job Bridge program in collaboration with your institution. This

program is designed to provide you with the practical skills and industry

experience needed to kick-start your career.

This is a limited-enrollment opportunity. We encourage you to register soon

to secure your spot.

To apply, fill out the form at this link: Our HR team will reach out to

shortlisted candidates for the next steps.

Apply Here:- https://forms.gle/xAjLBrVPp2FRrDsM8

https://forms.gle/xAjLBrVPp2FRrDsM8

For additional information, join our WhatsApp group:

https://chat.whatsapp.com/JKAouyKSlFdJ6SJjGoIKOm

https://chat.whatsapp.com/GIXHaFgp4DN29nA0ZCCbm0

https://chat.whatsapp.com/EVDhpVcQNky7Hfe8nv6LDt

------------------------------

Program Details

This program is structured into two distinct phases to ensure a

comprehensive learning experience:

 -

 Month 1: Training: This phase includes live lectures and mentorship from

 industry professionals to build a strong theoretical foundation. No

 prior knowledge or prerequisites are required. You will receive login

 credentials after registration.

 -

 Month 2: Internship: You will apply your knowledge to real-world

 industry projects. The internship includes:

 -

 Individual Projects: You will complete 10 individual projects, each

 with a dedicated mentor to guide you.

 -

 Capstone Project: This is a group project (10-12 interns per group)

 where you will work as a team on a larger, more complex problem.

Essential

 data and resources will be provided.

Flexible Learning Options

We understand that you have a busy schedule, so we offer flexible session

formats:

 -

 Mentor-led/Live Sessions: For a more interactive experience. You will

 attend live Zoom classes 3-4 times per week after 7 PM, with access to

 session recordings.

You'll also have 6-month access to our Learning Management System (LMS)

portal.

Career Benefits and Certifications

 -

 Program Completion Certificate: You will earn a certificate from UNLOX

 verified by SKILL INDIA AND STARTUP INDIA. This makes your certificate

 tamper-proof and easily verifiable by employers, proving the authenticity

 of your achievement.

 -

 Co-Branded Internship Certificate: Your internship certificate will

be co-branded

 with a multinational corporation (MNC). This collaboration adds

 significant value to your resume, as it demonstrates that your skills and

 project work meet the standards of a leading industry player.

 -

 Globally Recognized Certifications: You’ll be getting awarded by

 Prestigious from NASSCOM ( Govt. of India Ministry of Electronics and IT)

 -

 Placement Assistance: It means our team will provide continuous

support until

 you are placed. This includes:

 -

 Resume and Portfolio Building: We'll help you create a professional

 resume and portfolio that highlights the projects you've completed.

 -

 Interview Preparation: You'll participate in mock interviews and

 receive personalized feedback to boost your confidence.

 -

 Job Referrals and Networking: We'll connect you with our network of

 hiring partners and schedule interviews on your behalf.

subject: Paper Seeing, Revaluation and Re-FAT Process for Fall Semester 2025-26 (Regular & Week End Intra Semester) FAT – Theory
body:
Ref.No. : VIT/CoE/2025/25017

 Date: 17-December-2025

Paper Seeing, Revaluation and Re-FAT Process for

Fall Semester 2025-26 (Regular & Week End Intra Semester) FAT – Theory

 Paper Seeing and Revaluation:

· In the VTop student login, (“Examination → Marks → Fall

 Semester 2025-26”) Marks for the Courses to which FAT was held during

Nov-Dec 2025 has been made available now.

 Marks not displayed for the courses will be released within

this week

· Actual Grades will be released on 24 December 2025

(Wednesday). The Pass criteria and Grading Procedure are available in

Academics → Regulations Tab in your login.

· If you want to know the question wise marks awarded to your

answers by the evaluator, you need to apply for it through V-Top. This is

referred to as the “Paper Seeing” process. It requires payment of Rs. 100

for each paper. You can apply through: Examinations →Papersee/Rev → Fall

 Semester 2025-26→Paper Seeing. You can choose the course(s) you want

to apply for paper seeing. After Generating the Invoice, you need to make

a payment through the “Online Payments” Tab in the same V-Top login.

· Once you have paid, after 24 hours, the paper and question wise

marks awarded will be made available in CodeTantra login. You need to use

the same portal https://vit.codetantra.com for this process.

After seeing the paper, if you feel the mark awarded to a particular

question is not sufficient and the evaluator has missed something and there

is a need to recheck the mark, then you can apply for Revaluation of the

Course. You need to give suitable reasons for the same in the comments

section available just below the mark awarded by the faculty.

· Please note that the Revaluation has to be applied only in V-Top

(in the same way as you have applied for paper seeing) and necessary

payments also need to be paid through the online payments tab. (Rs. 300

per paper). Revaluation approval process in codetantra will be initiated

only after publishing the Grades, until then the status remains ‘approval

pending’ . Paper seeing and feedback / comments are mandatory for

re-evaluation and

are in online mode only.

 · Also note that “Paper seeing” and Revaluation is applicable

only for the Theory Courses to which FAT was conducted by the CoE office .

For other components and Courses (like Laboratory / Project Courses IBL

mode courses) there is No Paper seeing and Revaluation Process.

· The students who were involved in Fall Semester 2025-26

examination malpractices are not eligible for the paper

seeing/ Re-valuation process.

Particulars

Dates

Paper seeing registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 100]

 17-Dec

2025 to 22- Dec2025

Revaluation registration link / payment [per paper Rs. 300]

 18-Dec 2025 to 23- Dec-2025

Paper Seeing in https://vit.codetantra.com/

https://vit.codetantra.com/

 18- Dec-2025 to 23- Dec-2025

 Once the Paper seeing request is approved, the evaluated copy of answer

sheets would be made available in CodeTantra as per the above schedule.

Use your VTop login credentials for login.

· After login, follow the instructions given in the platform for

giving comments to the questions which need to be re-examined.

· Give your feedback with respect to the need for revaluation. If

no feedback is given for any question, your answer script will not be

considered for revaluation and No refund will be given for any approved

requests.

· Students should not approach or give any sort of request to any

faculty related to revaluation (increase of marks or grades). If we

receive any complaints from faculty, it will be treated as ‘Malpractice’

and revaluation requests will summarily be rejected.

Re-FAT:

As per VIT Academic regulations (Page 22) Re-FAT will be permitted for the

following reasons only:

S. No.

Description

Supporting Evidence(s) Required

1.

Calamity in the family [Death of father / mother / own brother / sister]

Death certificate or Prior communication to the Proctors

2.

Hospitalization of the student

(for in-patient treatment only)

Medical Certificate, Investigation Report, Bills and Discharge Summary.

· Eligible students should apply in VTop student login (

Examination > Re-Exam Application) between 5th January 2026 and 18th

January 2026 and upload the necessary evidence.

· Re-FAT requests will be scrutinized by the School Dean and then

by the ‘Re‐examinations Committee’. If needed the student may be asked to

appear before the Committee for presenting the case.

· For the ReFAT approved courses the Grade assigned will be

converted to “---“ by February end. ReFAT will be scheduled along with the

Winter 2025-26 Regular Arrear and the Regular Arrear Process will be

followed for Re-FAT.

· Any student who fails to apply for Re‐FAT through VTop will NOT

be considered for further processing and has to repeat the course(s) by

registering again in subsequent semesters.

· Please note that this process is only for getting approval

for Re-FAT. After it is approved, students need to register in Arrear

/ Re-FAT Tab for registering the course when it is permitted. The

schedule will be available only in Arrear/ Tab. If someone misses the

approved Re-FAT, no second chance will be given, and it will be treated as

absent accordingly, and the grade will be published.

Make-up Examination:

A separate circular will be issued by the COE regarding the registration

process for Make-up examination on 5th January 2026 (tentatively).

Controller of Examinations

With Regards

Prof.S.Sivabalan Ph.D

Controller of Examinations

Vellore Institute of Technology ( VIT)

Vellore 632014, TN, India

subject: Updated Placement Norms – 2027 Batch
body:
Placement Norms – 2027 Batch

Company Selection

Eligibility for further placements/internships

Selected by IT Services Companies (Internship/Fulltime)

1. Will be eligible for 1.5X CTC offer and above

(Applicable for IT Services / IT Product Companies)

Selected by any company for placements

1. Will be eligible for 2X CTC offer and above

2. Will be eligible for Dream (Core) offer

Selected for internship by IT product company (if the CTC on conversion is

more than 10 LPA) or termed as Super Dream Internship

1. Eligible for companies (Placements / Internship + Placements)

if the CTC is more than 2X and above

2. Eligible for companies(only placements) if the CTC is less

than 10 LPA

Selected for an internship by IT product company if the CTC is less than 10

LPA or termed as Dream Internship

1. Eligible for companies (Placements / Internship + Placements) if

the CTC is 2X and above (IT services / IT product)

2. Eligible for companies(only placements) if the CTC is

Less than 6 LPA

Selected in a Core Company for Non CS only

Will be eligible for 2X CTC only

Note:

1. Super Dream(Internship), Dream(Internship), Dream(Core) will be

specified in the placement notice

2. Students who plan for higher studies are eligible to take only the

IT Services companies offer (CTC – less than 6 LPA). IT Services or

regular offer (Sales / BD) will be specified on top of the notice.

3. Students dropping the Dream/ Super Dream (internship/fulltime)

offer after selection, in any of the above categories will have to do one

additional course and they will also be not be allowed for further

placements

4. Students withdrawing from internship before /after joining the

company also will be considered as “dropping of offer”

 Violation of PAT Norms:

1. Students planning for higher studies are not eligible for

Dream/Super Dream offers. They are allowed to attend only Software

services company’s interviews (Like TCS, Cognizant, Infosys etc.). VIT will

not issue “No Objection certificate” or recommendation letters to those

students who get selected in Dream /Super dream companies and later plan to

pursue their higher education. Dream /Super dream companies will be

notified in PAT notices.

2. Students who reject a Dream or Super Dream offer (Placement or

Internship) after getting selected have to do an additional academic course

to complete their degree requirements. The academic course has to be

completed in the final semester (no extension shall be given). The details

of the academic course to be completed will be shared by the Dean

(Academics) later. This also applies to the students who get Pre Placement

Offers after the summer internships. The earlier rule of not getting the

recommendation letter from the Professors for higher education also would

remain. "Once the higher PAT/CDC offer is declined by the student, all the

previous offers through PAT will also get cancelled/not considered"

3. Only registered students will be allowed for campus interviews and

other training programs organized by the placement centre. Those students

attending campus interviews without registering and not fulfilling the

eligibility criteria (as on date of selection test) would be summarily

rusticated from the University for Bringing Disgrace to the University.

4. It is found that Students who get placed in Dream or Super Dream

are violating the PAT norms and attending the off campus placements.

Students who get placed with on campus full time/internship placement

(dream or super dream) must accept the offer without fail and cannot

decline. Those who are going to get placed in Dream or Super Dream

placements should follow the PAT norms. Students who are violating the

norms will face severe disciplinary action.

Note:

All the companies allow students with no current backlogs for the selection

process.

PAT Category 

Category

Details

Category I

60 % in 10th, 12th, UG and PG as applicable and no year gap in studies.

Category II

60 % in 10th, 12th, UG and PG as applicable and upto 2 year gap in studies.

Category III

60 % in 10th /12th /UG and more than 2 year gap in studies.

Category IV

Less than 60 % in 10th /12th /UG and upto 2 year gap in studies.

Category V

Less than 60 % in 10th /12th /UG and more than 2 year gap in studies.

Gap in studies is counted from your Xth STD.

 Work experience is also counted as an academic gap.

Important Note:

1. Registration is purely voluntary.

2. It is informed that students in category III, IV and V may not

expect many companies as almost all the companies visiting VIT for Campus

Placement insist on 60% consistency and less than 2 years gap (i.e.

category I and II). Hence PAT registration is as per your

discretion/decision only.

3. All the companies allow students with no current backlogs /

required credits completed for the selection process.

4. Registration for other campus students will be done separately by

their respective campus.

5. N and F grades are considered to be backlogs by the industry.

Hence, it will be counted as current backlogs.

6. Please note that Placement registration fee once paid is NOT

REFUNDABLE.

All core companies

Note

1. IT Product company / IT Services Company / Core Company will be

subject: Information Session - Illinois Institute of Technology, USA-19 May - 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. (IST)
body:
Dear Students,

 The Office of International Relations at VIT is happy to share an exciting

opportunity to interact with representatives from Illinois Tech, USA!

We are thrilled to invite you to an invigorating Information Session on 19

May from 4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. (IST) over Zoom, where details about the

partnership between VIT Vellore and Illinois Institute of Technology will

be shared.

The session will cover partnership pathways and the benefits that can be

availed by you through this collaboration.

We request you all to kindly register using the link below:

https://apply.illinoistech.edu/register/?id=d33b0bb1-6a0c-4541-89f5-0d1426ac20a8

Please note that the Zoom link for the session will be shared one day

prior to the session with registered participants only. Therefore,

registration for the session is mandatory.

Here is a little something about Illinois Tech —

Why Study at Illinois Tech?

- Career-focused university in Chicago, a major U.S. hub for business,

technology, and innovation.

- Strong programs in engineering, computing, data, business, architecture,

and sciences.

- Ideal for students wanting practical learning and clear career outcomes.

Study in Chicago

- Learn in one of the most dynamic cities in the United States.

- Access to internships, networking, and employers across multiple

industries.

- Enjoy a true campus environment with easy access to downtown Chicago.

Career-Focused Education

- Curriculum designed to prepare students for real-world careers.

- Hands-on projects, research, internships, and co-ops support skill

development.

- Career Services supports resumes, interviews, and employer connections.

Strong Career Outcomes

- Illinois Tech publishes career outcomes for both UG and GR students.

- Graduates move into jobs, further study, and strong next steps.

- Outcomes demonstrate good alignment between programs and the job market.

International Student Friendly

- Large international student community from many countries.

- Dedicated support for visas, arrival, and academic transition.

- A global classroom experience with peers from around the world.

Great Value for Your Investment

- Recognized for strong return on investment and long-term earnings

potential.

- Combines quality education with strong career outcomes.

- A compelling choice for students comparing cost and value.

Hands-On Learning

- Learning through labs, projects, research, and real-world problem solving.

- Opportunities to apply classroom concepts to practical challenges.

- Builds confidence and employability.

Supportive Student Experience

- Support services for academics, careers, and international needs.

- Opportunities to join clubs, activities, and campus events.

- Helps students grow personally and professionally.

Why Students Choose Illinois Tech

- Chicago location and industry access.

- Strong STEM and career orientation.

- Welcoming international environment.

- High value and clear outcomes after graduation.

We look forward to your participation in the session and to supporting you

in exploring exciting academic pathways ahead.

subject: Call for Students Organizers/Managers/Coordinators/Volunteers for Riviera'25- Reg
body:
We at Vellore Institute of Technology-VIT Vellore believe that education is

not limited to the classroom but goes beyond. To facilitate this, VIT

conducts an Annual International Sports and Cultural Carnival Riviera that

strives to break every barrier, breach every limit, and

exceed every expectation year after year. With a footfall of more than

60,000 students from 70 different countries, it is with immense pleasure

and pride that we announce our next edition, RIVIERA 2025!

As we gear up for the next edition of RIVIERA, scheduled from 20th

February to 23rd February 2025, we are seeking enthusiastic individuals

who are eager to contribute their skills, creativity, and energy to create

an unforgettable experience for all participants.

We would like to invite applications from students for the post

of Student Organisers, Managers, Coordinators, and Volunteers for Riviera

‘25.

To apply, please fill out the form: https://forms.gle/VzZLaB9XvdquEuzY7

Deadline: 17th November 2025, Sunday 12:00 PM

The eligibility criteria are mentioned below:

1. Vellore Institute of Technology hosts two international

fests every year; those who have worked as Student Organizers in any one

fest, should not take part to give a fair chance to other students.

 2. Students’ Council members will not be considered for organizing

 positions. However, their services will be used appropriately.

 3. Academics requirements:

 Organizers should have at least 8.0 CGPA

 Managers should have at least 7.5 CGPA

 Coordinators should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 Volunteers should have at least 7.0 CGPA

 4. Physical attendance below 70% is not eligible for any of the posts.

 5. Students with standing arrears are not considered for any of the

 posts.

 6. Students who are involved in any disciplinary actions are not

 eligible. Even if he or she paid the fine, it is considered a disciplinary

 action.

 7. A student can be an Organizer/Manager if he/she has worked within

 the organizing committee of previous fests in the past year and has done

 considerable work. This needs to be acknowledged by the faculty coordinator

 of the concerned committee.

 Coordinators must have prominent contributions in clubs/chapters or in

 organizing any other event.

 Volunteers need not have prior experience.

 8. Students planning to do their project outside VIT are not eligible.

 9. If selected for the organizing team, the student should abide by the

 rules and regulations of the Riviera team.

 10. Only final-year students are eligible for the post

 of Student Organizer.

 Both final-year and pre-final-year students can apply for the post of

 Manager.

 Only pre-final year students can apply for the post of coordinator.

 Second-year students, the joining batch of 2023, are eligible only for

 the post of Volunteers.

 11. Only applicants who have completed the “Preferences for ProShow

 lineup” form sent by the Riviera’ 25 Convenor are eligible to apply for any

 post.

https://forms.gle/nbJV8WeZPGXzhzFL8

Join us in creating memories that will last a lifetime and fostering an

international community that celebrates diversity and unity. We look

forward to welcoming you to the RIVIERA family!

With warm regards

Dr K Gokul kumar

Professor-SMEC-VIT

Convenor-Riviera 25

subject: Clubs & Chapters Enrollments - Reg.
body:
Dear Students,

Greetings!

The wait is over and it's time to enroll for the VIT Clubs and Chapters!

Hope you all attended Quanta 2023 and got to know more about the

activities of our various Clubs and Chapters functioning under the Office

of Students' Welfare.

Students can now register for their preferred Clubs & Chapters for the year

2024.

NO maximum limit for enrolling in clubs/chapters.

Clubs & Chapters enrollment is valid only for ONE year.

Registration can be done through VTOP- SW Events- Club/Chapter

Enrollments.

Select the check box against your preferred Club & Chapter and submit.

A Green Tick against your selected CC means that you have been enrolled.

Please ensure that the registration process is completed before logging out.

For any queries, please mail to events.sw@vit.ac.in <events.sw@vit.ac.in> 

Last Date for Enrollment: 09.02.2024 (Friday)

subject: Best wishes for your exams from V-HAPPY
body:
Dear Students,

Greetings from the Centre for VIT Happiness and Well Being (V-HAPPY) !!!

It is natural to feel stressed or anxious during exams, but remember that

your sincere effort, persistence and commitment towards preparation for

your exams is meaningful and truly matters the most at this time. Exams are

a reflection of your learning, perseverance, dedication and determination

towards your potential goal. While you focus on your exams, do remember to

take care of your well-being: rest for a while when needed, stay hydrated

and keep a positive mindset. A calm mind supports a confident performance.

If at any point of time, you feel stressed, overwhelmed, anxious or simply

wish to talk to someone, our Counsellors are here for you. You are not

alone-and you never have to handle things by yourself. Reaching out is a

sign of strength. Our Counsellors are available to listen, support and

guide you in a safe and confidential space. Please feel free to connect

with us on the details given below:

Dear Nayan Sharma, 

Your MATLAB license entitles you to try prereleases when available. The R2026a prerelease is now available. 

Download Prerelease https://www.mathworks.com/downloads/prerelease?s_v1=62686&elqem=4960491_EM_WW_DIR_25-10_R2026a-PRERELEASE-GENERAL&rec_id=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&elqTrackId=e71238d4c7d6406f97f7b34a02cb7f93&elq=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&elqaid=62686&elqat=1&elqCampaignId=24191&elqak=8AF5F0B65FE3D486495A6304570448B5BC9FD59623F0B2F7828D9DD11D73A4A3E4B6 

The R2026a prerelease includes new features in MATLAB and Simulink, and updates to all other products. You are eligible to download the prerelease of all your licensed products. For more information about the prerelease, see the release highlights https://www.mathworks.com/products/new_products/release-highlights.html?s_v1=62686&elqem=4960491_EM_WW_DIR_25-10_R2026a-PRERELEASE-GENERAL&rec_id=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&elqTrackId=1515eb28fac64e0ebdd6e1b5ccb6b5a7&elq=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&elqaid=62686&elqat=1&elqCampaignId=24191&elqak=8AF5631F0EC8C8891CE75471F01B66B0A995D59623F0B2F7828D9DD11D73A4A3E4B6 and release notes https://app.go.mathworks.com/e/er?s_v1=62686&elqem=4960491_EM_WW_DIR_25-10_R2026a-PRERELEASE-GENERAL&rec_id=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&s=646005169&lid=42530&elqTrackId=3bc962889c02462ebfcff005ec201bdf&elq=b56618464e694f02800ecb50b85d7e1d&elqaid=62686&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5ADB7EAAC47E719FA9DF4975B9B0F78ECD59623F0B2F7828D9DD11D73A4A3E4B6. 

New features include:

MATLAB 

Java Runtime: Install your own version of compatible OpenJDK releases. 

Python Integration: Use the External Languages panel to view, create, and manage Python environments in MATLAB; automatically convert MATLAB string arrays to a Python list or NumPy string array.

Sharing from MATLAB Drive: Share files and apps stored in MATLAB Drive directly from the MATLAB Desktop and App Designer, respectively.

Simulink 

New Rich Context Menus: Access actions from a simplified context menu that is built for discoverability and filters options based on the tools you are using.

Compare and Merge Data Dictionaries: Compare Simulink Data Dictionaries (SLDD) to identify differences in design data, configuration sets, and more; merge desired changes into a new target SLDD file.

Model Reference Rebuild: Customize the default rebuild behavior for new models to avoid unnecessary compilations.

After downloading, you will receive a survey where you can provide feedback ahead of the release. We look forward to hearing from you about this new release of MATLAB and Simulink. 

Sincerely,

subject: FALL SEMESTER 2025-26 THEORY FAT INSTRUCTIONS
body:
Dear Students,

INSTRUCTIONS TO STUDENTS APPEARING FOR FALL SEMESTER 

 2025-26 THEORY FAT

General Instructions

· Students must enter the examination hall 15-30 Minutes before

the commencement of examination (between 9.00 - 9.15 AM )

· You need to WEAR Student IDENTITY CARD during the ENTIRE

EXAMINATION PERIOD. If you don’t have a Proper ID Card contact the

Registrar Office and apply for a new one and get it before coming to the

Exam. The ID card should be scratches free with a proper tag. Exchange of

ID cards or Tags will be considered as Malpractice. If you have misplaced

your ID card or forgot to bring it to the Examination Hall, Report to the

Control Room (PRP 115/SJT G01/TT 104) of your test venue to get One Time

Permit Slips. You need to pay Rs. 100 through V-TOP online payment only.

· You will NOT be permitted to use the toilet/washroom during the

examination, so be prepared for it.

· Exchange of Calculators, Stationeries, Code Books, pen, pencil

etc., are not permitted. The code Books or standard tables should have been

signed by either the faculty or School office. No markings of any kind

should be found in such booklets.

· As per VIT rules, even if you keep your mobile phone/smart watch

in a switched off position inside the examination hall, it will be treated

as examination malpractice. Such malpractices will lead to confiscation of

the devices (including SIM card) for one semester and ’N’ grade (ALL PAPER

ZERO) in all the registered courses including lab & project components in

that semester. Hence, before entering the examination hall, students should

check their pockets thoroughly to avoid carrying mobile phones/smart

watches by mistake.

· Possession of any Electronic Gadget (Mobile Phone, Smart Watch,

Bluetooth device, any device embedded with scanner /camera, etc.), holding

chit papers/ suspicious content in the examination hall is considered as

malpractice.

 A. Pre-Exam Activities

1.

Note down your seating arrangement (Building, Room Number and Seat Number)

from the V-TOP students login. Seating arrangement will not be displayed

for courses in which a student has been debarred. Please report yourself

half an hour prior to the exam. No student would be permitted to enter the

hall after 9.15 AM.

2.

Possession of unauthorised material, even if you do not intend to use it

will be considered as malpractice. Before starting the exam, check any

materials written on desks or walls, or found papers nearby/ around you in

the floor and inform the same to the invigilators.

B. During the exam

1.

Candidate has to sit in the allotted seat only. Listen to the invigilator

and follow their instructions at all times. Strict Silence should be

maintained in the examination hall. Discussions/ communications of any kind

inside the exam hall are treated as examination malpractices.

2.

Check the class number in the Question paper with the Attendance sheet

Class Number. If you have not received the right question paper or

incomplete or badly printed, please contact the invigilator immediately. If

you have any doubt on class number, course name, course code, slot, and any

other details related to your question paper, please check while signing in

the attendance sheet.

3.

Read carefully and follow the instructions printed in the question paper

and in the answer booklet.

4.

Fill required details (Register No., course code, course title etc.) in the

answer booklet before you start writing the exam. After signing in the

attendance sheet, check the barcode sticker pasted on your answer booklet

for its correctness as your answer booklets will be scanned for valuation

using this barcode only.

5.

First clearly write the Question number in the space provided and then

start writing your answers. USE BLUE / BLACK PEN ONLY for writing the

Answers. Writings on any thin pens, / light colours may not be visible on

the scanned images used for evaluation. Remember to write the answers

within the space provided in the answer booklet. If you write anything

outside the margin, it will be cut during the scanning process. If you are

using extra sheets like graph sheets / templates given by faculty, write

your answer booklet number alone on the top left edge outside the margin

and keep it immediately after the first sheet. Do not fold it as it needs

to be scanned for valuation. Do your rough work in the last page of the

main answer booklet itself. Before finishing the exam, strike out all the

rough works.

6.

Don’t write anything in the question paper or in your hand or leg or on a

desk or on walls nearby you.

7.

Correcting pens, fluid or tape and erasable pens are not to be used for

corrections in the answer booklet.

8.

Do not discuss / borrow anything with other candidates during the

examination.

9.

Do not get involved in any unfair or dishonest practice during the exam. If

you try to cheat or break the rules in any way, it will invite appropriate

sanctions under malpractice.

10.

Students are not allowed to ask questions of any kind during the

examination. Invigilators have been instructed not to answer any enquiry

whatsoever relating to the question papers, whether an explanation or

meaning or correction or typographical error

11.

On the day of the exam, if you feel that you are affected by ill health,

please contact the Chief Superintendent or Invigilator. You can write the

examination at the Health Centre.

12.

Do not leave the examination hall until told to do so by the invigilator.

You cannot leave the examination hall until 30 min from the start of the

examination. If any student leaves the exam hall before 12.00 noon, he/she

has to submit the question paper along with answer sheet.

13.

Do not take your answer booklets or unused ones, from the examination hall.

It is a serious Malpractice.

14.

Answer booklet contains 42 pages and no additional sheets, no threads,

will be provided. 

C. If booked under Malpractice

1.

Be calm and give a written response to the allegation and follow the

instructions from the exam squad / Invigilator / Asst. CS / CS.

2.

Do not indulge in any disrespectful activities such as shouting / creating

/ diverting attention of all other students, a scene in the examination

hall.

3.

Hand over the materials and get a receipt for electronic devices.

NON-COOPERATION WILL BE VIEWED AS AN ACT OF INDISCIPLINE WHICH MAY INVITE

SEPARATE DISCIPLINARY ACTION.

4.

Examination malpractice actions/punishments are very serious, may lead to

All paper ZERO or suspension of one semester. All malpractice actions are

informed to the students / published in VTOP student Login. Please go

through it follow the examination rules appropriately

5.

OBEY ALL THE EXAMINATION RULES SERIOUSLY

With Regards

Prof.S.Sivabalan Ph.D

Controller of Examinations

Vellore Institute of Technology ( VIT)

About us: VISA is not a Bank or a credit card company! VISA is the

world's leader in digital payments technology which offers Financial

Technologies. Visa's mission is to connect the world through the most

creative, reliable, and secure payment network - enabling individuals,

businesses, and economies to thrive. Our advanced global processing

network, VisaNet, provides secure and reliable payments around the world,

and is capable of handling more than 65,000 transaction messages a second.

The company's dedication to innovation drives the rapid growth of connected

commerce on any device and fuels the dream of a cashless future for

everyone, everywhere. As the world moves from analog to digital, Visa is

applying our brand, products, people, network, and scale to reshape the

future of commerce. (More information can be found on : Visa, a trusted

leader in digital payments. https://www.visa.co.in/)

Details: 

Job Title:

Software Engineering Intern (Summer Internship)

Job Description:

Please find Attached

Job Location:

Bengaluru

Eligibility:

CGPA≥7.0

No active backlogs

Eligible batch:

2027

Eligible streams:

CSE/ECE/IT/EEE/SW/Mathematics &Computing

Eligible programs:

B.E/B.Tech

Min. 10 weeks mandatory internship

Early May'26 - mid July'26

Selection Procedure:

Online test (coding round) followed by 1 technical interview

Stipend & Benefits

Details

Amount (INR)

Visa provides all-rounded work experience to provide an enriching

Internship experience, access to exciting projects and career building

exposure.

90,000

95,000

Benefits

Details

Relocation

1,00,000 INR

hackathons, career development and skill development workshops,

Experiential learning with on-the-job training

Access to office cafeteria

In-house breakfast & lunch

Gym, Office transport, snacks, In-house recreational centers

Free of cost

Insurance

Covered

All the benefits of your employment with Visa will be governed by

policies, procedures and guidelines of Visa, which are subject to change

from time to time, at the sole discretion of the management without giving

any notice or assigning any reason thereof"

 Candidates whose primary residence is located within a 30-mile radius of

the designated Bangalore office shall not be eligible for relocation

assistance. Eligibility for this benefit will be strictly determined based

on the residential address stated in the government-issued identification

document submitted at the time of official offer letter issuance.

Note: Request the students to share their personal email IDs who are

applying for this role at VISA. We require these email IDs to facilitate

hassle-free communication with the candidates throughout the

Recruitment/Onboarding process process.(Please DO NOT change email IDs

till the end of hiring process with VISA)

Interested and eligible students can register in the below link on or

before 10th September 2025 3.00 pm without fail.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [12th June] 

 events

The World Day Against Child Labour

The World Day Against Child Labour, which is held every year on June 12, is

intended to foster the worldwide movement against child labor. The

International Labour Organisation (ILO) launched the World Day Against

Child Labor in 2002. Since then, the day has focused attention on the

prevalence of child labor throughout the world and the action and efforts

essential to eliminating it. Around the world, there are 152 million

children in child labor; 73 million of them are engaged in hazardous work

that directly harms their health, safety, or moral development. The

International Labour Organization defines child labor as "work that

deprives children of their childhood, their potential, and their dignity,

and that is harmful to physical and mental development." Not all work done

by children is child labor. Activities that contribute to a child’s

positive development and provide skills and experience for them to become

productive members of society are not child labor.

Children around the world are routinely engaged in paid and unpaid forms of

work that are not harmful to them. However, they are classified as child

laborers when they are either too young to work, or are involved in

hazardous activities that may compromise their physical, mental, social, or

educational development. In the least developed countries, slightly more

than one in four children (ages 5 to 17) are engaged in labor that is

considered detrimental to their health and development.

protect children’s rights and highlight the importance of supporting

affected children. Follow us, engage in trivia, attend the session, test

labor on June 12th, 2024, and advocate for a better future for all children.

Labour: Unite for Children's Rights", a quiz which will be conducted

Child Labour.The event aims to raise awareness about the issue of child

labor and advocate for children's rights. Participants will engage in a

eradicating child labor globally.

subject: Invitation to Participate in NextEdge 1.0 - a Tech Talk on BioFab 3D - YANTRA'26
body:
Dear VITians,

The Office of Students' Welfare is pleased to invite you all to the NextEdge

1.0 – a Tech Talk on BioFab 3D, organised as a part of Yantra’26. This

event is aimed at exploring the fascinating world of 3D Bioprinting,

where cells, bioinks, and smart scaffold design come together to mimic life

itself.

The session will be headed by Dr. Gopal Shankar from NIT Calicut, a VIT

alumnus (B.Tech. in Biotechnology, 2009), featuring his transformative

research insights, real challenges, and what it really takes to turn

biology into engineered tissues, offering students an excellent opportunity

to learn, interact, and gain inspiration from the expert.

This is a limited-opportunity session to learn, interact, and gain

perspectives that can add real value to your academic and professional

journey. Look for ideas, exposure, and inspiration that many students

actively seek.

We encourage you to register using the Google Form link given below to

secure your spot for this exceptional opportunity.

Registration Link: https://forms.gle/4QC6PmhZBvK6AW4f9

Event Details:

Date: 13th February, 2026

Time: 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM

Venue: Channa Reddy Auditorium

Looking forward to your enthusiastic participation.

subject: Congratulations to Team 3Blue1Brown on Their Achievement at FinAgent Hackathon, Techfest 2025, IIT Bombay
body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that Team 3Blue1Brown has brought laurels to

VIT by securing 1st Place at the FinAgent Hackathon, conducted as part

of IIT Bombay’s Techfest 2025, held from 22nd to 24th December 2025.

During the final round of this prestigious national-level hackathon, with

the final presentation held on 22nd December 2025, the team presented

their agentic-AI product to a distinguished jury that included C-suite

executives from Jio Finance. In recognition of their outstanding

performance and innovation, the team was awarded a cash prize of ₹50,000.

Team Members:

 - Meda Varshith Kumar Reddy (23BCE0614)

 - Rohit Phaniram Sakamuri (23BDS0051)

 - Aniruddha Neema (23BIT0282)

 - Harshvardhan Dayanand (24BCI0096)

We also extend our sincere appreciation to Dr. Pradheep Thiyagarajan (Emp.

ID: 15266) for his invaluable guidance and continuous support, which

played a crucial role in the team’s success.

Congratulations once again to Team 3Blue1Brown on this remarkable

achievement!

I am happy to inform you that our Library and CTS teams have successfully

upgraded the RemoteXs (E-Gateway) platform to the MyLOFT app-based access

system. The platform is now fully functional on mobile phones, laptops,

and desktop computers, providing seamless access to our electronic

resources anytime, anywhere.

I sincerely appreciate the dedicated efforts of the Library and CTS teams

in resolving the compatibility issues overnight and ensuring a smooth

transition to the new platform.

I also extend my heartfelt thanks to the entire VITians for your patience,

cooperation, and support throughout the upgradation process.

I encourage you to explore our vast collection of e-resources and make the

neighbour.

subject: Call for Abstracts: ICFMFT-2025 - Request to participate and disseminate the conference call
body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Greetings from the Centre for Functional Materials, VIT, Vellore. Hope this

email finds you well.

It is my pleasure to invite you to participate at the 2nd International

Conference on Functional Materials for Future Technology (ICFMFT-2025),

scheduled to be held from 5th to 7th November 2025 at Vellore Institute

of Technology, Vellore, India. This is the second edition of the series of

conferences started in 2023.

Keynote address by renowned professors and eminent scientists from India

and abroad. A few confirmed speakers are mentioned below:

Dr. Satoru Yoshimura, Akita University, Japan

Dr. Ramamoorthy Ramesh, Rice University, USA

Dr. Ramesha K, Director CECRI, Karikudi

Dr. R. Kothandaraman R. IIT Madras, India

Dr. François Courvoisier, CNRS, FEMTO-ST institute, France

Dr. Tamalika Banerjee, University of Groningen, The Netherlands

Dr. Sayani Majumdar, Tampere University, Finland

Dr. Sumeet Walia, RMIT University, Australia

Dr. Shweta Agarwala, Aarhus University, Denmark

Dr. Ren, Wei, Shanghai University, China

Dr. Satheesh Krishnamurthy, University of Surrey, UK

Dr. M. S. Ramachandra Rao, IIT Madras, India

Dr. P. Saravanan, DMRL, Hyderabad, India

Dr. N. Vijayan, NPL, New Delhi, India

Dr. B. B. Lahari, IGCAR, Kalpakkam, India

Dr Ashis Kumar Panda, CSIR, NML, Jamshedpur, India

IC-FMFT 2025 https://vit.ac.in/conference/IC-FMFT-2025/ mainly focuses on

topics related to Functional Materials for Future Technologies. The

conference will feature plenary talks, technical sessions, poster

presentations, and opportunities for collaboration and networking. Conference

also includes oral and poster presentations and awards for the

participants. Further, selected presentations and posters will be included

in the special issue of a Scopus-indexed journal(s).

Publishing Partners: Wiley; Springer

•Small Methods (IF. -9.1)

•Particle & Particle Systems Characterization (IF. -3.0)

•Journal of Electronic Materials (IF. -2.5)

•Physica Status Solidi – RRL (IF. - 2.0)

Oral and Poster Presentation Awards sponsors

•RSC Advances

•RSC Materials Advances

•Wiley

•ACS

•VIT

Important Dates:

Abstract Submission: Open

Registration: Open

Early Bird Registration Ends: 10th October 2025

For more information and Group Registration Discounts, please visit the

conference website or write to us at:

Email: icfmft@vit.ac.in

Conference Website: IC-FMFT 2025

https://vit.ac.in/conference/IC-FMFT-2025/

Registration Link: https://events.vit.ac.in/

We hereby invite you and request you to circulate the conference brochure

to your department and research fraternity.

Thank you, and we look forward to your active participation at ICFMFT-2025.

With regards

Organizing Committee

ICFMFT-2025

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dr Madhuri W 

Professor and Director 

Centre for Functional Materials 

Vellore Institute of Technology 

Vellore 632014

Tamil Nadu, India.

Greetings!

The Office of Students' Welfare presents an evening filled with

performances full of talent and fun.

SOLO DANCE PRELIMS

Natya: Dance filled with colourful folk dances and energetic Bollywood

movies. This Prima Vera 2023, we present to you a Solo Dance: Eastern

Competition, Natya! Come join us and witness some brilliant

performances.

Piroutte: Be it locking, popping, or hip-hop, we've got it all covered.

Come, join us at Pirouette: the western solo dance competition, and

witness some power-packed performances!

Date: 02.11.2023

Time: 11:00 AM onwards

Venue: CS Hall

SOLO VOCAL PRELIMS

Sargam: The prelims of Eastern Solo Music Competition: Sargam, an

exclusive solo singing competition between talented eastern vocalists from

the 2023 batch of VIT! Whether you’re trained or not, talent has its own

way of unveiling itself. So join us in the prelims and be a part of the

amazing musical showdown!

Crescendo: Be it country, pop, or any other genre of western music,

talented vocalists can convey so much in just a few words. Here's your

chance to stand out and show us what you are made of! Show us your musical

prowess in crescendo and stand a chance to win exciting prizes!

Date: 02.11.2023

Time: 02:00 PM onwards

Venue: Rajaji Hall

HAND PAINTING: HOKO DOKO

“HOSO DOKO”, is another exciting art event where you can pick up your

tools and create another masterpiece. Today, we are excited to present to

you our live painting competition for our talented artists! Come join us

for a scintillating experience! Participate, explore, and enjoy!

Date: 02.11.2023

Time: 02:00 PM onwards

Venue: Anna Auditorium

DIGITAL PAINTING: E:ASEL

"Creativity is like sand, the tighter you hold it, the more will it flow

out."

Forms of art have grown through the years, from paper to walls there has

not been any surface where our creativity can't be seen, Then why leave

alone your tablets? Office of Students' Welfare brings to you "E:asel:

Digital Painting Competition" where you can let your creativity and

thoughts flow on the Digital Canvas. So what are you waiting for get your

digital pens out and let the art flow!

Date: 02.11.2023

Time: 04:00 PM onwards

Venue: MB 210

PHOTOGRAPHY: ISITHOMBE

"A picture is a poem without words"

Photography has been revered for its ability to transfer people into the

world of imagination, where you can enjoy the aroma of scenic landscapes or

feel the rage of war. The Office of Students' welfare presents to you

"ISITHOMBE:

A Photography Competition" where you can showcase your talent with

breathtaking photographs. Brace up and adjust your lenses to bring out the

best of your potential!

Date: 02.11.2023

Time: 02:30 PM onwards

Venue: CS Hall

SHORT FILM MAKING : EIGA

Film making gives the ability to foster creativity and give individuals an

opportunity to portray their emotions, opinions and social concerns through

the visual media. The Office of Students' welfare presents to you "Eiga: A

Short Film Competition" where you can showcase your talent with some

remarkable directives in film making!

subject: Yantra'26 Central Hack Registration is Live - Reg
body:
Dear VITians,

Yantra’26 is back with Central Hack, designed to bring together the

brightest minds, boldest ideas, and most passionate problem-solvers from

diverse academic backgrounds.

With the prize pool of INR 6,00,000+, Yantra Central Hack is a

flagship 56-hour

hackathon organized by the Office of Students’ Welfare, bringing

together participants from diverse disciplines to collaborate, innovate,

and solve real-world challenges while fostering teamwork, creative

problem-solving, and technical excellence in an intense, fast-paced

environment, scheduled from 13th February to 15th February at the Anna

Auditorium.

The official Central Hack website is LIVE now at: Central Hack Official

Portal

http://central-hack.vit.ac.in/?utm_source=mail&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=central_hack_mail

Round 0 has officially kicked off!

So this is your cue to gear up, assemble your team, and get ready to make

your mark.

Important Instructions

 -

 The Team Leader must register first, share the team code, and ensure

 all team members complete registration and join the team.

 -

 Teams must consist of 3–5 members, with at least one female

 participant mandatory.

 -

 Submissions must be made only in the provided template format: Submission

 Template

 https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1PmilmBDYnUZfzc7KVS1u2QRH6Dm5Xs71-BI881SeMzw/edit?usp=sharing

 -

 Submissions must be shared in the form of a Google Drive link on the

 Central Hack Portal.

 -

 Ensure the Drive link has open access (Anyone with the link can view).

 -

 Incomplete submissions or restricted-access links will not be evaluated.

Deadlines

 -

 All Round 0 submissions must be completed before the specified deadline

 on the Central Hack portal.

 -

 Late entries will not be considered under any circumstances.

Stay tuned, stay curious, and stay ready - because Yantra Central Hack is

where ideas turn into impact.

See you at the hackathon. Let the countdown begin.

students across India. This hackathon, now in its third successful cohort,

offers participants the chance to solve real-time technical problems, win

industry leaders and recruiters, and explore various aspects of

ServiceNow's technology, culture, and career paths.

effectively.

subject: Additional Learning Concept _ reopened from Winter 2023 - 24 onwards
body:
Dear All,

The provision for awarding marks to the students under “Additional

Learning” component will be enabled on “VTOP Faculty Login” from the

forthcoming Winter 2023 -24 onwards. The required details are provided

below:

In order to make student learning capabilities more meaningful and activity

oriented, programmes like Hack-a-thons, Make-a-thons and other similar

activities

can be conducted on campus. In order to integrate this in academics,

additional marks can be awarded to the student by the faculty after due

assessment of the performance of the student. The student can get benefitted

by such additional marks, to a maximum of 20, which can be added to the CAM

score for one course per semester. Allotment of such additional marks is

subject to conditions that (1) the activity should have been scheduled for at

least 24 continuous hours, (2) monitored by the faculty who is offering the

course related to the activity, (3) the team size should not be more than

three and (4) the assessment done in one semester cannot be used / forwarded

to the subsequent semesters. The allotment of the marks may vary from 5

(just participation) – 20 (prize winner) depending on the involvement and

output of the student in the event as per the details given below. The

faculty handling the course will award the marks based on the performance

of the student. If a student wishes to do a project in courses and results

with tangible output can also be considered for additional marks.

Participation throughout the event and active involvement

5 Marks

Tangible output/result producers

10 Marks

Considerable amount of creative input in the outcome

15 Marks

Prize/award winners of the event

20 Marks

In any case, prior approval from the faculty handling the course and the

School Dean is essential for the inclusion of additional marks for such

categories. This additional learning is course specific. It is the

responsibility of the School to make sure that additional marks are

allotted to only one course for a specified activity. The total internal

marks (including the additional marks) is given an upper limit of 60 (40

being the marks given to the final assessment test).

Mere performance of routine experiments should not be considered for

additional marks.

Attending “online Courses”, “Workshops / Seminars” organized by any

institute are not to be considered for additional marks.

Since the award of marks is a sensitive matter, any violation of the

academic regulations will be viewed seriously. Moreover, the faculty

members may also note that the “Additional Learning” is only an option and

it is at the discretion of the respective faculty members to use this

component for awarding marks.

with regards

M. Anthony Xavior PhD

Dean Academics

Vellore - 632014

subject: Invitation for Two Days Hands-on Workshop on RISC-V VEGA PROCESSORS - November 8-9, 2024
body:
Two Days Hands-on Workshop on

 RISC-V VEGA PROCESSORS FOR IoT APPLICATIONS

 (India’s Indigenous

Processor Developed by C-DAC)

 November 8-9, 2024

 organized

by the

 School of Electronics

Engineering, VIT Vellore

 in

association with

 Centre for Development of Advanced Computing

(C-DAC), Thiruvananthapuram

Key Highlights:

The workshop covers everything from the initial setup of VEGA processors to

the detailed operation of various sensors, including LDRs, RFID, BMP, IR,

and more.

Participants will explore practical applications of these sensors, such as

using Light Dependent Resistors (LDRs) for automatic lighting control and

infrared (IR) sensors for motion detection, object detection, and proximity

sensing.

REGISTRATION:

CATEGORY-1 – Rs.1500/- (Rs. 1271 +GST) (inclusive of ARIES V3.0 board

https://www.amazon.in/VEGA-Processor-ARIES-Development-Board/dp/B0CTZWBDV3,

Registration Kit and refreshments) 

CATEGORY-2 - Rs.500/- (Rs. 423+GST) (Registration Kit and Refreshments)

Registration Link: https://events.vit.ac.in

A participation certificate will be provided to all the participants.

Registration Deadline: 27th October 2024. (Limited to 60 seats, first come

first serve basis).

About ARIES v3.0 Development Board ( https://amzn.in/d/6QBN6t0

https://amzn.in/d/6QBN6t0 )

ARIES v3.0 is a development platform based on THEJAS32 ASIC which operates

at a frequency of 100MHz. THEJAS32 SoC includes VEGA ET1031 Microprocessor,

256KB internal SRAM, Three UARTs, Four SPIs, Three TIMERs, Eight PWMs,

Three I2C interface, 32 GPIOs etc. This board contains everything needed to

support the standalone operation. To get started simply connect the board

to a computer with a USB cable or power it with a AC/DC adapter or a

battery.

This board is designed and developed by Centre for Development of Advanced

Computing (C-DAC) as part of the Microprocessor Development Programme

project funded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology,

Government of India. This board is targeted for a wide variety of

applications which includes low power IoT, Sensor fusion, Smart Meter,

System supervisors, Remote sensors, Wearable devices, Toy and electronic

education equipment, Legacy 8/16-bit applications, Industrial networking

and many more…

Resource Persons:

AVIN JOSEPH, Project Engineer C-DAC Trivandrum; HIMANSHU DIWANE, Project

Engineer C-DAC Trivandrum and CDAC Team

For more details, please get in touch with the course coordinator,

Prof.Jayakrishanan

(pjayakrishnan@vit.ac.in; +91 9944243462)

With Thanks and Regards,

Prof. Sivanantham S

Dean, School of Electronics Engineering

VIT, Vellore 632014

subject: Live Project in Data Science & Machine Learning with Python
body:
Hi ,

We're pleased to open applications for the Finlatics Data Science & Machine Learning Experience Program, an online live project that helps students gain experience in data science with Python and using machine learning algorithms at Vellore Institute of Technology.

This project runs at leading campuses, including IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, and BITS Pilani. Finlatics and was incubated at the Atal Incubation Centre, supported by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog and Government of India.

STRUCTURE of the Live Project:

1. Learn the basics of Python and Machine Learning and how it can be used in data science.

2. Get hands-on learning and experience in writing various Python codes.

3. Dive into practical data manipulation and visualization using essential Python libraries.

4. Become proficient in using the Google Colab Notebook for machine learning

5. Gain an understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms using Python libraries

6. Explore statistical methods crucial for accurate data analysis, empowering learners with essential analytical skills.

7. Complete industry-specific case projects to understand the application of Python and Machine Learning in business scenarios

The project is doable along with any other commitment due to its work-from-home and online structure

Student OUTCOMES:

1. Certificate of Work Experience in Data Science

2. Letter of Recommendation on performance

3. A Certificate of Proficiency i n Python and Machine Learning

To apply, students can fill out the form below, and we will get in touch with them:

https://www.finlatics.com/bads_application?utm_src=vitv

As Python would be taught in the program, all students must note that no prerequisites or prior domain knowledge are required to be a part of the program.

Personalized guidance & mentoring would also be provided to help students learn Python.

Live Sessions will be provided to help you practice coding with Python.

Project Duration: 2 months (3-4 Hours per week)

Project Start: Flexible on selected student choice.

Project Break & Extension: Selected students will be eligible for a break or extension during the project if needed for any exams, assignments, or personal commitments.

If selected, the program has a minimal induction fee of Rs. 1999 + GST / Rs. 2999 + GST (on student choice)

Fee Waiver: Vellore Institute of Technology students will be given a 20% fee waiver on the above mentioned minimal induction fee.

To be eligible for the waiver, kindly apply via the link above.

We are excited to have a fruitful engagement.

subject: Université de Tours -France- International exchange students - Nominations S2 2025/26
body:
Kind Attention: Pre-Final Year Students

The University of Tours will be opening the nomination period for

mobilities taking place during the second semester of the 2025/26 academic

year (January – May) next month, on the 6th of October 2025.

In order for you to have a holistic overview upon the aspects connected to

this topic, please find a list of useful information enumerated below.

Why choose the University of Tours for your semester abroad in France?

 - Course on offer

 - Online course catalogue (-> course name, credits, content, hours,

 coordinator, level) – disciplinary courses

Students can use our online catalogue, that lists the most popular courses

(French/English) for exchange students: Course Catalogue for Exchange

Students. https://cces.univ-tours.fr/Accueil.php?language=EN

Beyond disciplinary courses taught in French, UT provides also students

with more than 150 courses in English in different fields (Humanities,

Science and Technology). Only a beginner-intermediate level of French is

required if your students choose disciplinary courses taught in English.

They have the right to choose courses in any discipline (from all faculties

apart from medicine), provided the conditions of our interinstitutional

agreement are fulfilled (the majority of their classes must be taken within

a specific field of studies, for example), that both their academic

coordinators approve it, and that their home university will recognize the

credits obtained in a different discipline than the student’s major at the

end of the mobility, these credits being relevant to the student’s academic

project.

 - French language and culture classes

Exchange students can complete their learning agreement with French courses

https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students/6-learn-french-cuefee-crl

 provided by our University Center of Teaching French to International

Students (CUEFEE), labeled with a maximum three stars

https://www.univ-tours.fr/international/le-cuefee-renouvelle-son-label-qualite-fle-avec-3-etoiles

by

the French Government for the quality of its teaching and services

Students can select up to 3 courses (up to 72 hours), that are

completely free of charge for exchange students. Each course will give

students 4 ECTS, as follows:

§ Written language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Oral language (24h/semester), 4 ECTS credits

§ Cultural options (20h/semester), 4 ECTS credits (from B1 level on)

Classes are taught beginning with the A1 CEFR level in French to C1. This

is the main scheme for international exchange students.

 - Individual support

The University of Tours assists international exchange students prior to

their mobility with every administrative aspect related to their arrival in

France, from the online pre-registration to the visa procedure (if

applicable), and facilitates their accommodation request in a public

student residency.

 - Visa – Campus France procedure for exchange students that are not

 European citizens (not a citizen of one of the 27 EU member states), or

 citizens of a Schengen / EEA country

 - Accommodation – housing request for public student residencies

 - Learning Agreement and online course catalogue

 - French language and culture classes

 - Academic calendar and timetable

 - Integration – For the integration of exchange students different

 resources exist in order to facilitate it

 - Orientation period: organised at the beginning of each semester,

 it allows students to discover the city, the university, and

to meet other

 students, both local and internationals

 - Buddy System: a French student to support them soon after their

 arrival in Tours

 - Erasmus Student Network https://www.facebook.com/ESNTours/: the

 association organizes cooking activities, international dinners, theme

 evenings. The membership gives access to preferential rates for the

 cultural events organized by the international relations

office of the UT

 and gives them the right to have discounts with the partners of the

 association (Ryanair, local stores…).

 - Cultural programme

 - International Relations Service organizes a great cultural

 programme

 https://international.univ-tours.fr/english-version/admission-process-for-exchange-students/10-culture-sports

for

 the students with visits to the chateaux of the Loire Valley and

 many other unmissable spots of the region and France.

 - In addition, the cultural service of the university organizes

 many cultural events and offers discounts to the students who have the

 cultural pass (opera, cinema, shows…).

 - Sports

§ Students have access to a wide variety of sports at the UT

https://www.univ-tours.fr/campus/accueil-sport-1. They can subscribe to

the Pack’Sport and take up to 3 different sport classes a week, absolutely

free of charge! They can also do sports trainings during week-ends on

different themes (hiking at the Mont-Saint-Michel, canyoning, skiing…) and

attend sport events or wellness activities (badminton, fitness night,

rugby…).

o Orientation maps

§ A map of UT’s campuses, faculties, and student services

https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?mid=1Oe2Q_yuy9VbAkhtfCiHYJhzh8K8iYXA&usp=sharing

§ A map allowing students to discover the city

https://www.google.com/maps/d/viewer?mid=1KeCNJLFEccVbzUZTNfD3VfNAz-ktLv0&ll=47.38009226217868%2C0.688595800000007&z=13

from

an extracurricular point of view

· Warm welcome

As a token of hospitality and deep interest in student welfare, students

are welcomed individually upon their arrival to help them finalize their

administrative registration, and give them all the practical information

they need for their settling in (presentation of the different useful

university services, organized events, information about the ESN, public

prioritising mobilities that fit within our framework, in order to avoid

any unpleasant situation for the selected students (example: if your second

semester starts in February / March, you can prioritize mobilities starting

in September; we would be delighted to welcome your students for a complete

academic year)

subject: SW Newsletter_February 2024 - Reg.
body:
Dear VITians,

“Though February is short, it is filled with lots of love and sweet

surprises.” - Charmaine J. Forde

February is an interesting month. It might not be the most glamorous month

in the calendar but February has its charms.

The month kicked off with the Annual NSS Special Camp in Vandranthangal

village, Katpadi. Various programmes like surveying, training the self help

group, teaching the school kids which included awareness and motivational

talks, tree plantation, medical camp, etc were conducted. The Camp was

inaugurated by the VIT Chancellor, Vice Presidents, Pro-VC, Registrar, VAO

& other village leaders.

An orientation programme was organized by the VIT Standards Club on 6th

February 2024 that aimed to educate the members about the crucial standards

landscape, with a focus on the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Dr. Baskar

A., Technical Consultant, Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances Limited was the

Chief Guest for the session.

The Installation Ceremony of the Rotaract Club saw the new leadership

outline their vision for 2024. Mr. Hemant Sahal, Founder and CEO of Digii

(formely CollPoll) was invited to provide insights on Viksit Bharat 2047.

The month also witnessed the much awaited cultural extravaganza,

Riviera'24, with various cultural and sports events. Pre-Riviera events

like Agaaz, Kalaa etc. offered wonderful experience and entertainment to

the students. The Proshows saw some of the maestros like Shankar Mahadevan,

Vijay Prakash, G V Prakash, Saindhavi, Sathyprakash and Band Agam perform

their hit numbers.

To read about more such events and activities, check out our newsletter!

subject: Congratulations to VIT Debate Society on their Achievement at Manzar 2026 – Miranda House, University of Delhi
body:
Dear VITians,

We are delighted to share that the VIT Debate Society achieved notable

recognition at Manzar 2026, the annual flagship British Parliamentary (BP)

debating tournament hosted by the English Debating Society of Miranda

House, University of Delhi, held from 21–23 February 2026.

Manzar is one of the prominent debating tournaments on the Indian debating

circuit, bringing together leading debaters and adjudicators from various

institutions across the country. Representing VIT with distinction, our

participants engaged in rigorous rounds of parliamentary debate and

adjudication.

Achievement Secured:

 1. Shivansh Choukse (24MIS0266) – Adjudicator Break: Novice Semifinals,

 Open Pre-Quarterfinals, and Open Semifinals (Adjudicated 3 out of 4

 outrounds in the tournament)

This accomplishment highlights the analytical ability, debating expertise,

and adjudication excellence demonstrated by the members of the VIT Debate

Society on a prominent national debating platform.

We sincerely acknowledge the invaluable guidance and continuous support of

the Faculty Coordinator, Prof. Anil Premraj (Emp. ID: 12531), whose

mentorship significantly contributed to this achievement.

We extend our heartfelt congratulations to the VIT Debate Society on this

commendable achievement and wish them continued success in their future

endeavors.

Dear VITians,

The Office of Students’ Welfare invites you for today’s [4th June] events.

International Day of Innocent Children Victims of Aggression

International Day of Innocent Children Victims of Aggression is a United

Nations observance held on June 4 every year. It was established on 19

August 1982. Originally focused on victims of the 1982 Lebanon War, its

purpose expanded to "acknowledge the pain suffered by children throughout

the world who are the victims of physical, mental and emotional abuse. This

day affirms the UN's commitment to protecting the rights of children. All

over the world, when it comes to conflicts like wars, the ones who are

affected the most are the little ones – namely children. Unable to

understand or defend themselves, they are often the ones who suffer the

most pain whether it be physical, mental, or emotional.

The day signifies its acknowledgment of the pain suffered by children

throughout the world due to the physical, mental, and emotional abuse they

went through. The day also affirms the United Nation’s commitment to

protecting the rights of children the world over. It carries out its work

under the guidance of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which is

the most rapidly and widely ratified international human rights treaty in

history.

subject: Orientation session on 2+2 and 4+1 transfer program to University of Edinburgh, UK- Top Ranked University in the world.
body:
Dear Students,

This is to inform you that we will be orgainsing an orientation session on

the 2+2 and 4+1 transfer programs at the University of Edinburgh, UK, on

January 24 and 25 at 2:30 PM.

The session is open to interested students.

Date: 24th Jan'25

Time: 2:30 PM

Venue: Online Platform

https://ed-ac-uk.zoom.us/j/86187963067

Passcode: M6U3r8CZ

Timelines and requirements for applying to 2+2 and 4+1 are as follows.

Kindly note that the application deadline is 29th January and you will

need to apply through a system called UCAS

Following the submission of your application, the University of Edinburgh

will contact you to request these additional documents:

 - Official transcript

 - English language qualification (such as IELTS or TOEFL or Class XII

 English if you already have these – if not you will need to submit by 30

 th April)

 - List of courses you are currently studying but have not yet completed

 in Semester 4

You should aim to submit your supporting documents by 31st March 2025 but

you can submit your English language qualification later by 30th April 2025

if you do not have this yet.

You should be on track for an 80% or above GPA to be considered as well as

good grades in engineering-specific subjects.

Minimum English language requirements are 6.0 overall and 5.5 in each

component in IELTS (or equivalent). We are also pleased to offer a

scholarship of £3,500.00 per year for new students starting in 2025/26.

For details and interaction kindly login on above link and join the

session on 24th Jan'25 at 2:30 PM 

For more details, Please contact: 

Dr Raghuram, Asst Director IR

Dear VITians,

In celebration of International Women’s Day 2025, the Office of Student

Welfare, in collaboration with the Railway Protection Force, is organizing

a road play at Katpadi Railway Station to create awareness on women

empowerment among railway passengers.

This event will feature a mime and mono-acting performance by the Dramatics

Club of VIT, along with speech, Silambam, Parai, and dance performances by

PB-Tamil Literary Association.

Event Details:

Date: 07/03/2025

Time: 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM

Venue: Katpadi Railway Station

Join us in spreading awareness and celebrating the strength and resilience

of women through the performances!

subject: Congratulations to Ojasvi (23BBS0012) for Achievement at Saarang 2026 | IIT Madras
body:
Dear VITians,

We are pleased to share that Ojasvi (23BBS0012), a student member of the VIT

Dramatics Club, has secured the 2nd Runner-Up position at “Face of

Saarang”, a beauty pageant competition conducted as part of Saarang 2026,

the iconic cultural festival of IIT Madras on 10th January 2026.

The competition featured multiple rounds evaluating personality, stage

presence, confidence, ramp walk, and talent presentation. Ojasvi’s

background in theatre and dramatics significantly contributed to her

performance, particularly during the talent and expressive rounds, where

her acting skills, articulation, and stage command were key differentiators.

Along with achieving the 2nd Runner-Up position, she was also conferred

with the titles of “Best Ramp Walk” and “Best Use of Props”,

highlighting her poise, creativity, and overall performance excellence at a

prestigious inter-university platform.

We express our sincere appreciation to Dr. Mathumathy S (Faculty

Coordinator, Emp. ID: 16210) for her continuous guidance, encouragement,

and support.

Congratulations to Ojasvi on this commendable accomplishment!

Dear Student of VIT,

Greetings from Mindenious.

This email is to inform you about Training and Internship Program available to students of VIT. The program focuses on skill development, practical exposure, and career preparation through structured online training and guided project work.

The training curriculum is designed with reference to industry practices commonly followed by organizations such as IBM, Microsoft, Deloitte, Cognizant, Infosys, Oracle, and Genpact, to help students gain relevant professional exposure.

Application Link: https://forms.gle/LfMUvXfBZ7oHQp91A

Referral Code: MIND30

Please note: Program training fees are applicable.

Program Overview

Duration: 2-3 Months

Mode: Online

Phase 1: Learning & Training

 Online sessions conducted by experienced trainers

 Interactive learning and doubt-clearing sessions

 Approximately 5-6 sessions per week

Phase 2: Project Work

 Practical project implementation with mentor support

 Individual Minor Project (7 days)

 Group Major Project (21 days)

Phase 3: Career Preparation

 Career guidance and placement support

 Resume preparation and interview practice

 Professional communication and soft-skills sessions

Program Benefits

 Access to recorded sessions via the learning platform

 Continuous mentorship throughout the program

 Participation in the Mindenious learning community

 Exposure to career opportunities through hiring partners

Certifications

 Internship Certificate issued by Mindenious and partner organizations

 Course Completion Certificate (ISO Certified)

 Performance-based Letter of Recommendation

 Excellence Certificate for notable performance

 Continued access to learning resources

Seats are limited. Scholarship options on the program fee may be available for eligible students.

subject: Applications for Student Council 2024-25 - Reg.
body:
Dear Students,

Greetings!

Are you a leader who wants to make a change?

The Office of Students' Welfare is currently seeking nominations for the

2024-2025 academic year.

The Student Council is a diverse group of students from across all

departments, working to represent the needs and aspirations of the entire

student body. If you're passionate about making VIT an even better place,

we encourage you to nominate yourself!

For more information on the nomination process and the role of the Student

Council, please visit the following links.

Google Form Links:

Executive & Member Secretary: https://forms.gle/PYkToeGdRDhT7QNc7

Secretary (Cultural & Technical): https://forms.gle/GME7hxTswz2kLdR57

Digital Support Team: https://forms.gle/Pc683RoM7NVvezET9

The link will be available only till 18.05.2024 (Saturday), 5:00 PM and

deactivated afterwards.

The applications received only through the google form will be scrutinized

and called for an interview.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: 

1. Only Final and Pre Final Year Students shall apply for the post of Executive

and Member Secretary.

2. Final Year Students to act as Executive Member and Pre Final Year

Students to act as Member Secretary.

3.

Executive & Member Secretary: 

 - For all 5 Year Programmes (B. Arch. and Integrated Programmes), only

 2020 and 2021 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 4 Year Programmes (B. Tech., B. Des. & B. Sc. Hons.), only

 2021and 2022 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of

 Executive Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 3 Year Programmes (B.B.A., B.Com. & B.Sc.), only 2022 and 2023

 Year Students to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive

 Member & Member Secretary respectively.

 - For all 2 Year Programmes (M. Tech. & M.Sc.), only 2023 Year Students

 to be considered eligible for the posts of Executive Member.

4. Students from all years are eligible to apply for the post of Secretary

(Cultural & Technical) and Digital Support Team Member.

5. Minimum of 9 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post of

Student Council Member.

6. Minimum of 8.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Secretary (Cultural & Technical).

7. Minimum of 7.5 CGPA required for a student to be eligible for the post

of Digital Support Team Member.

8. Students involved in any disciplinary issues, currently or in the past,

are not eligible for holding any post.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF STUDENT COUNCIL MEMBERS: 

· To officially represent all the students in the school / institute.

· To identify and help solve problems encountered by students in the

school / institute.

· To communicate its opinion to the school / institute administration on

any subject that concerns students.

· To promote and encourage the involvement of students in organizing

school / institute level activities.

· To inform students about any subject that concerns them.

· To consult students on any issue of importance and bring it to the

notice of the Students' Welfare office.

· To support and contribute to achieve better / higher accreditation for

the institute.

· To participate in the development of the school activities.

· To propose activities to the school/institute administration that would

improve the quality of student life in the school/institute.

We look forward to receiving your nominations!
